translations.literal: Wei Siqian
translations.idiomatic: Wei Siqian

sentences.zh: （子承慶嗣立）

translations.literal: (His sons Chengqing and Silizhi succeeded him.)
translations.idiomatic: (His sons Chengqing and Silizhi carried on his line.)

translations.idiomatic: (His son Xiangxian.)

translations.idiomatic: Su Gui

translations.idiomatic: (His son Ting.)

sentences.zh: 韋思謙，鄭州陽武人也。

translations.literal: Wei Siqian was a native of Yangwu in Zheng Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Siqian came from Yangwu in Zheng Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 本名仁約，字思謙，以音類則天父諱，故稱字焉。

translations.literal: His original name was Renyue, and his style was Siqian; because it resembled the taboo name of Empress Wu's father, he used his style name.
translations.idiomatic: His birth name was Renyue, but he went by his style Siqian, since the former sounded too close to the taboo name of Empress Wu's father.

sentences.zh: 其先自京兆南徙，家於襄陽。

translations.literal: His ancestors had moved south from Jingzhao and made their home in Xiangyang.
translations.idiomatic: His family had migrated south from the Jingzhao region and settled in Xiangyang.

sentences.zh: 舉進士，累補應城令，歲餘調選。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi examination, was repeatedly appointed magistrate of Yingcheng, and after a year or more was transferred for selection.
translations.idiomatic: After taking his jinshi degree, he served repeatedly as magistrate of Yingcheng; a little over a year later he entered the regular rotation for promotion.

sentences.zh: 思謙在官，坐公事微殿，舊制多未敘進。

translations.literal: While Siqian was in office he received a minor demotion for an official matter; under the old regulations many in such cases were not promoted.
translations.idiomatic: Siqian had incurred a slight demotion over an official matter, and under the old rules such men were usually passed over for advancement.

sentences.zh: 吏部尚書高季輔曰：“自居選部，今始得此一人，豈以小疵而棄大德。”

translations.literal: Minister of the Ministry of Personnel Gao Jifu said, "Since I took charge of selection, this is the first time I have obtained such a man—how could I discard great virtue for a small flaw?"
translations.idiomatic: Gao Jifu, Minister of Personnel, said, "In all my time running selection, this is the first man of his caliber I have seen. How could I reject great merit over a trifling fault?"

sentences.zh: 擢授監察御史，由是知名。

translations.literal: He was promoted and appointed investigating censor, and thereby became well known.
translations.idiomatic: Siqian was promoted to investigating censor and soon made a name for himself.

sentences.zh: 嚐謂人曰：“御史出都，若不動搖山嶽，震懾州縣，誠曠職耳。”

translations.literal: He once said to someone, "When a censor leaves the capital, if he does not shake mountains and rivers and awe prefectures and counties, he has truly neglected his duty."
translations.idiomatic: He once remarked, "A censor who leaves the capital without shaking the hills and terrifying the districts has plainly failed in his post."

sentences.zh: 時中書令諸遂良賤市中書譯語人地，思謙奏劾其事，遂良左授同州刺史。

translations.literal: At that time Zhongshu Ling Chu Suiliang disdained and sold land belonging to a translator of the Secretariat; Siqian memorialized and impeached him for it, and Suiliang was demoted to prefect of Tong Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: When Chief Minister Chu Suiliang sold off Secretariat translators' land at a contemptuous price, Siqian impeached him, and Suiliang was demoted to prefect of Tong Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 及遂良復用，思謙不得進，出為清水令。

translations.literal: When Suiliang was restored to favor, Siqian could not advance and was sent out as magistrate of Qingshui.
translations.idiomatic: Once Suiliang returned to power, Siqian found his career blocked and was posted out as magistrate of Qingshui.

sentences.zh: 謂人曰：“吾狂鄙之性，假以雄權，觸機便發，固宜為身災也。

translations.literal: He said to people, "My wild and coarse nature, given bold authority, stirs at the first provocation—I was bound to bring disaster on myself."
translations.idiomatic: He told others, "Give my rash, uncouth temperament real power and I strike at the first provocation—disaster for myself was only to be expected.

sentences.zh: 大丈夫當正色之地，必明目張膽以報國恩，終不能為碌碌之臣保妻子耳。”

translations.literal: A great man should stand where his countenance is upright, open his eyes wide and repay the state's grace; in the end he cannot be an undistinguished official who merely protects wife and children.
translations.idiomatic: A true man belongs where he can show an honest face and repay the throne openly and boldly—not end as some timid clerk clinging to wife and children."

sentences.zh: 左肅機皇甫公義檢校沛王府長史，引思謙為同府倉曹，謂思謙曰：“公豈池中之物，屈公為數旬之客，以望此府耳。”

translations.literal: Zuo Su-ji Huangfu Gongyi, inspecting and confirming as chief administrator of the Prince of Pei's palace, invited Siqian as joint administrator of granaries of the same palace, and said to Siqian, "You are surely no creature of a mere pool—I have employed you as a guest for a few score days in anticipation of this establishment."
translations.idiomatic: Huangfu Gongyi of the Left Su-ji, acting as chief administrator of the Prince of Pei's household, brought Siqian in as granary officer and told him, "You are no fish for a shallow pond—I only keep you here a few weeks as a guest until this household can rise to your stature."

sentences.zh: 累遷右司郎中。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to director of the right bureau.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through several posts to director of the right bureau.

sentences.zh: 永淳初，曆尚書左丞、御史大夫。

translations.literal: In the beginning of the Yongchun era he successively served as left vice director of the Secretariat and censor-in-chief.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of the Yongchun period he served in turn as left vice director of the Secretariat and as censor-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 時武候將軍田仁會與侍御史張仁禕不協而誣奏之。

translations.literal: At that time Military Guard General Tian Renhui was on bad terms with Attending Censor Zhang Renyi and made a false accusation against him.
translations.idiomatic: Military Guard General Tian Renhui, feuding with Attending Censor Zhang Renyi, lodged a false charge against him.

sentences.zh: 高宗臨軒問仁禕，仁禕惶懼，應對失次。

translations.literal: Emperor Gaozong came to the hall and questioned Renyi; Renyi was fearful and flustered, and his answers were confused.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gaozong questioned Renyi in open court; terrified, Renyi answered incoherently.

sentences.zh: 思謙曆階而進曰：“臣與仁禕連曹，頗知事由。

translations.literal: Siqian came up the steps and advanced, saying, "I served in the same office with Renyi and know rather well how the matter stands."
translations.idiomatic: Siqian mounted the steps and said, "I served with Renyi in the same office and know the facts fairly well.

sentences.zh: 仁禕懦而不能自理。

translations.literal: Renyi is timid and could not clear himself.
translations.idiomatic: Renyi is too timid to defend himself.

sentences.zh: 若仁會眩惑聖聰，致仁禕非常之罪，即臣亦事君不盡矣。

translations.literal: If Renhui should dazzle and delude Your Sagely Hearing and bring Renyi to an extraordinary punishment, then I too would have failed in serving my lord.
translations.idiomatic: If Renhui should mislead Your Majesty and bring Renyi to an extreme penalty, then I too would have failed in my duty to the throne.

sentences.zh: 請專對其狀。”

translations.literal: I request to answer solely regarding the facts of the case.
translations.idiomatic: I ask leave to answer the charge on the facts alone."

sentences.zh: 辭辯縱橫，音旨明暢，高宗深納之。

translations.literal: His argument was free and unrestrained, his tone and meaning clear and fluent; Emperor Gaozong deeply accepted it.
translations.idiomatic: His reply was forceful and lucid, and Emperor Gaozong took it to heart.

sentences.zh: 思謙在憲司，每見王公，未嚐行拜禮。

translations.literal: While Siqian was in the Censorate, whenever he saw kings and dukes he never performed bowing courtesy.
translations.idiomatic: In the Censorate, Siqian never bowed when he met princes or dukes.

sentences.zh: 或勸之，答曰：“雕鶚鷹鸇，豈眾禽之偶，奈何設拜以狎之？

translations.literal: Some urged him; he replied, "Eagles, hawks, and falcons—how could they be mates of common birds? Why perform bowing to be familiar with them?"
translations.idiomatic: When others urged him, he answered, "Are eagles and falcons companions of barnyard fowl? Why bow and make yourself familiar with them?

sentences.zh: 且耳目之官，固當獨立也。”

translations.literal: Moreover, an official of ears and eyes should properly stand apart.
translations.idiomatic: Besides, the censor is the ruler's eyes and ears—he ought to keep his distance."

sentences.zh: 初拜左丞，奏曰：“陛下為官擇人，非其人則闕。

translations.literal: When he first took office as left vice director, he memorialized, saying, "Your Majesty selects men for office; if they are not the right men the post remains vacant."
translations.idiomatic: On first taking office as left vice director, he memorialized: "Your Majesty chooses the man for the post, and leaves the post empty rather than fill it with the wrong man.

sentences.zh: 今不惜美錦，令臣製之，此陛下知臣之深，亦微臣盡命之秋。”

translations.literal: Now you spare no fine brocade and command me to cut it—this is Your Majesty's deep knowledge of me, and also the season when this humble subject must exhaust his life.
translations.idiomatic: Now you hand me fine brocade and bid me cut the garment—this shows how deeply Your Majesty knows me, and it is the moment when your servant must give his all."

sentences.zh: 振舉綱目，朝廷肅然。

translations.literal: He raised and set in order the statutes and ordinances, and the court was solemnized.
translations.idiomatic: He restored order to the statutes, and the court grew grave and disciplined.

sentences.zh: 則天臨朝，轉宗正卿，會官名改易，改為司屬卿。

translations.literal: When Empress Wu held court, he was transferred to director of the imperial clan; when official titles were changed, it was changed to director of imperial dependents.
translations.idiomatic: When Empress Wu took power, he became Director of the Imperial Clan; when titles were revised, the post was renamed Director of Imperial Dependents.

sentences.zh: 光宅元年，分置左、右肅政台，復以思謙為右肅政大夫。

translations.literal: In the first year of Guangzhai, the left and right Su-Zheng platforms were separately established, and Siqian was again made right Su-Zheng grandee.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Guangzhai the Left and Right Su-Zheng platforms were split apart, and Siqian was again named Right Su-Zheng Grandee.

sentences.zh: 大夫舊與御史抗禮，思謙獨坐受其拜。

translations.literal: The grandee had formerly stood on equal ceremonial footing with censors; Siqian alone sat and received their bows.
translations.idiomatic: By old custom the grandee and the censors exchanged equal courtesies; Siqian alone remained seated and accepted their bows.

sentences.zh: 或以為辭，思謙曰：“國家班列，自有差等，奈何以姑息為事耶？”

translations.literal: Some took exception; Siqian said, "The state's ranks and positions have their own gradations—how can one make indulgence the business?"
translations.idiomatic: Some objected, but Siqian said, "The court has its ranks—why make indulgence your policy?"

sentences.zh: 垂拱初，賜爵博昌縣男，遷鳳閣鸞台三品。

translations.literal: In the beginning of Chuigong, he was granted the title baron of Bochang, and promoted to third rank of Fenige Luantai.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Chuigong era he was made Baron of Bochang and promoted to third rank in the Fenige Luantai.

sentences.zh: 二年，代蘇良嗣為納言。

translations.literal: In the second year he replaced Su Liangsi as chief counselor.
translations.idiomatic: In his second year he succeeded Su Liangsi as chief counselor.

sentences.zh: 三年，上表告老請致仕。

translations.literal: In the third year he submitted a memorial reporting old age and requesting retirement.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year he memorialized his advanced age and asked to retire.

sentences.zh: 許之，仍加太中大夫。

translations.literal: It was granted, and he was additionally given grand master of palace counsel.
translations.idiomatic: The request was granted, and he was further honored as Grand Master of Palace Counsel.

sentences.zh: 永昌元年九月，卒於家，贈幽州都督。

translations.literal: In the ninth month of the first year of Yongchang, he died at home; posthumously appointed regional commander of Youzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He died at home in the ninth month of the first year of Yongchang and was posthumously named regional commander of Youzhou.

sentences.zh: 二子：承慶、嗣立。

translations.literal: Two sons: Chengqing and Silizhi.
translations.idiomatic: He had two sons: Chengqing and Silizhi.

sentences.zh: 承慶，字延休。

translations.literal: Chengqing, styled Yingxiu.
translations.idiomatic: Chengqing, styled Yingxiu,

sentences.zh: 少恭謹，事繼母以孝聞。

translations.literal: In youth he was respectful and cautious, and was known for filial piety toward his stepmother.
translations.idiomatic: was from youth respectful and careful, and won renown for treating his stepmother with filial devotion.

sentences.zh: 弱冠舉進士，補雍王府參軍。

translations.literal: At twenty he passed the jinshi examination and was appointed adjutant of the Yong Prince's palace.
translations.idiomatic: At twenty he took the jinshi degree and became adjutant in the household of the Prince of Yong.

sentences.zh: 府中文翰，皆出於承慶，辭藻之美，擅於一時。

translations.literal: All literary compositions of the palace came from Chengqing; the beauty of his rhetoric was unmatched in his time.
translations.idiomatic: Every document in the prince's household came from Chengqing's pen; for a time none could rival the grace of his prose.

sentences.zh: 累遷太子司議郎。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to remonstrator of the heir apparent's household.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through several posts to remonstrator in the heir apparent's household.

sentences.zh: 儀鳳四年五月，詔皇太子賢監國。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of the fourth year of Yifeng, an edict ordered Crown Prince Xian to oversee the state.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of the fourth year of Yifeng, Crown Prince Xian was ordered to supervise the realm.

sentences.zh: 時太子頗近聲色，與戶奴等款狎，承慶上書諫曰：

translations.literal: At that time the crown prince was rather given to music and women and was on intimate terms with household slaves and the like; Chengqing submitted a memorial of remonstrance, saying:
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince had grown fond of music and women and kept close company with household slaves; Chengqing submitted a memorial of remonstrance:

sentences.zh: 臣聞太子者，君之貳，國之本也。

translations.literal: I have heard that the crown prince is the ruler's second self and the foundation of the state.
translations.idiomatic: I have heard that the crown prince is the ruler's second self and the foundation of the state.

sentences.zh: 所以承宗廟之重，係億兆之心，萬國以貞，四海屬望。

translations.literal: Therefore he bears the weight of the ancestral temple and binds the hearts of the hundred millions; the myriad states look to him for constancy, and the four seas fix their hopes on him.
translations.idiomatic: He bears the weight of the ancestral shrines and holds the hearts of the myriad people; all lands look to him for steadiness, and the four seas fix their hopes upon him.

sentences.zh: 殿下以仁孝之德，明睿之姿，嶽峙泉渟，金貞玉裕。

translations.literal: Your Highness, with your benevolent and filial virtue and your bright and discerning bearing, stands like a mountain peak and rests deep as a spring, firm as gold and generous as jade.
translations.idiomatic: Your Highness combines benevolence and filial piety with bright intelligence—steady as a mountain, deep as a spring, firm as gold, generous as jade.

sentences.zh: 天皇升殿下以儲副，寄殿下以監撫，欲使照無不及，恩無不覃，百僚仰重曜之暉，萬姓聞洊雷之響。

translations.literal: The Heavenly Sovereign raised Your Highness as heir designate and entrusted you with oversight and nurture, wishing that your illumination reach nothing left unlit and your grace extend without exception; the hundred officials look up to the radiance of the heavy star, and the myriad people hear the rolling sound of repeated thunder.
translations.idiomatic: His Majesty has raised you as heir and entrusted you with oversight of the realm, that your light may leave nothing in shadow and your grace reach every corner; officials look to you as to a second sun, and the people listen for your voice as for rolling thunder.

sentences.zh: 夫君無民，無以保其位；

translations.literal: For a ruler without the people cannot preserve his position;
translations.idiomatic: A ruler without the people cannot keep his throne;

sentences.zh: 人非食，無以全其生。

translations.literal: and people without food cannot preserve their lives.
translations.idiomatic: and the people without food cannot live.

sentences.zh: 故孔子曰：“百姓足，君孰與不足；

translations.literal: Therefore Confucius said, "When the common people have enough, who alone will the ruler lack enough?"
translations.idiomatic: Confucius said, "When the people have enough, how can the ruler alone lack?

sentences.zh: 百姓不足，君孰與足？”

translations.literal: When the common people lack enough, who alone will the ruler have enough?"
translations.idiomatic: When the people lack, how can the ruler alone have enough?"

sentences.zh: 自頃年已來，頻有水旱，菽粟不能豐稔，黎庶自致煎窮。

translations.literal: In recent years there have been frequent floods and droughts; grain and millet have not yielded abundantly, and the common people have brought themselves to destitution.
translations.idiomatic: In recent years floods and droughts have come again and again; harvests have failed, and the people have been driven to destitution.

sentences.zh: 今夏亢陽，米價騰踴，貧窶之室，無以自資，朝夕遑遑，唯憂餒饉。

translations.literal: This summer's fierce heat has sent grain prices soaring; poor households have no means to support themselves and from morning to evening live in anxiety, fearing only famine.
translations.idiomatic: This summer's drought has sent grain prices soaring; poor families cannot support themselves and live from hour to hour in dread of famine.

sentences.zh: 下人之瘼，實可哀矜，稼穡艱難，所宜詳悉。

translations.literal: The afflictions of those below are truly pitiable; the hardships of farming ought to be understood in detail.
translations.idiomatic: The suffering of the humble is truly pitiable, and the hardships of the fields deserve your close attention.

sentences.zh: 天皇所以垂衣北極，殿下所以守器東宮，為天下之所尊，得天下之所利者，豈唯上玄之幽讚，亦百姓之力也。

translations.literal: The reason the Heavenly Sovereign drapes his robes at the northern pole and Your Highness guards the vessel in the eastern palace, that you are honored by all under heaven and gain what all under heaven gains, is not only the hidden praise of supreme heaven but also the strength of the common people.
translations.idiomatic: His Majesty rules from the north and you guard the heir's charge in the eastern palace; the honor and benefit you receive from the realm come not from heaven alone but from the people's strength as well.

sentences.zh: 百姓危，則社稷不得獨安。

translations.literal: When the common people are in peril, the altars of soil and grain cannot alone be secure.
translations.idiomatic: When the people are in peril, the state cannot stand secure by itself.

sentences.zh: 百姓亂，則帝王不能獨理。

translations.literal: When the common people are in disorder, the emperor and king cannot alone govern.
translations.idiomatic: When the people fall into disorder, the throne cannot govern alone.

sentences.zh: 故古之明君，飽而知人饑，溫而知人寒，每以天下為憂，不以四海為樂。

translations.literal: Therefore the enlightened rulers of antiquity, though sated, knew when others hungered, and though warm, knew when others were cold; they always took all under heaven as their worry and did not take the four seas as their pleasure.
translations.idiomatic: The sage rulers of old, though well fed, knew others starved; though warm, knew others froze; they made the realm their worry, not the four seas their playground.

sentences.zh: 今關、隴之外，凶寇憑淩，西土編，凋喪將盡，干戈日用，烽柝薦興，千里有勞於饋糧，三農不遑於稼穡。

translations.literal: Now beyond the passes of Guan and Long, fierce bandits press upon the borders; the registered people of the western lands are nearly exhausted by loss, arms are employed daily, beacon fires rise in succession, for a thousand li there is toil in supplying grain, and the three classes of farmers have no leisure for sowing and reaping.
translations.idiomatic: Beyond Guan and Long fierce enemies press the frontier; the people of the west are dying off, war is daily, beacon fires never cease, supply lines strain for a thousand li, and farmers have no time left for the fields.

sentences.zh: 殿下為臣為子，乃國乃家。

translations.literal: Your Highness is both minister and son—both state and family.
translations.idiomatic: You are at once a subject and a son—the state and the family rest on you alike.

sentences.zh: 為臣在於竭忠，為子期於盡孝。

translations.literal: As minister lies in exhausting loyalty; as son lies in fulfilling filial piety.
translations.idiomatic: As a subject you must give your utmost loyalty; as a son you must fulfill your utmost filial duty.

sentences.zh: 在家不可以自逸，在國不可以自康。

translations.literal: At home one may not indulge ease; in the state one may not indulge comfort.
translations.idiomatic: At home you may not indulge ease; in the realm you may not indulge comfort.

sentences.zh: 一物有虧，聖上每留神念；

translations.literal: If any single thing falls short, the sage sovereign always keeps his mind upon it;
translations.idiomatic: If anything goes wrong, His Majesty always takes it to heart;

sentences.zh: 三邊或梗，殿下豈不兢懷。

translations.literal: if the three frontiers are obstructed, how can Your Highness fail to be vigilant in mind?
translations.idiomatic: if the frontiers are blocked, how can Your Highness fail to be vigilant?

sentences.zh: 況當養德之秋，非是任情之日。

translations.literal: Moreover, this is the season for cultivating virtue, not the day for indulging one's desires.
translations.idiomatic: This is the season to cultivate virtue, not the time to follow whim.

sentences.zh: 伏承北門之內，造作不常，玩好所營，或有煩費。

translations.literal: I venture to learn that within the northern gate construction is unceasing, and what is undertaken for pleasure may entail troublesome expense.
translations.idiomatic: I understand that within the palace there is unceasing construction, and your amusements may entail wasteful expense.

sentences.zh: 倡優雜伎，不息於前，鼓吹繁聲，亟聞於外，既喧聽覽，且黷宮闈。

translations.literal: Singers, actors, and miscellaneous performers cease not before you; drums and pipes with their dense sounds are constantly heard outside; they both disturb what reaches your ears and profane the inner palace.
translations.idiomatic: Singers, actors, and variety performers never leave your sight; drums and pipes sound without cease; they deafen the court and profane the inner quarters.

sentences.zh: 兼之仆隸小人，緣此得親左右，亦既奉承顏色，能不恃托恩光。

translations.literal: Moreover, menial slaves and petty men, by this means gain closeness at your side; having once attended to your countenance, how can they fail to rely on and trade on your favor?
translations.idiomatic: Servants and petty men use these pleasures to draw near you; once they have won your favor, they will surely trade on your grace.

sentences.zh: 作福作威，莫不由此，不加防慎，必有愆非。

translations.literal: To dispense blessings and wield authority—all comes from this; if you do not add precaution, there will surely be fault and wrong.
translations.idiomatic: Blessing and authority alike flow from such company; without caution, wrongdoing is sure to follow.

sentences.zh: 儻使微累德音，於後悔之何及？

translations.literal: If your virtuous reputation should suffer the slightest stain, how could regret afterward avail?
translations.idiomatic: If your good name should suffer the slightest blemish, what use will regret be afterward?

sentences.zh: 《書》云：“不作無益害有益。”

translations.literal: The Documents says, "Do nothing unprofitable that harms what is profitable."
translations.idiomatic: The Book of Documents says, "Do not do what is useless to the harm of what is useful."

sentences.zh: 此皆無益之事，固不可耽而悅之。

translations.literal: These are all unprofitable matters and surely must not be indulged in and delighted in.
translations.idiomatic: These are all useless pursuits and must not be indulged or enjoyed.

sentences.zh: 臣又聞“高而不危，所以長守貴；

translations.literal: I have also heard, "High yet not perilous—thereby one long preserves nobility;"
translations.idiomatic: I have also heard, "Stand high yet avoid peril, and you may long keep your nobility;

sentences.zh: 滿而不溢，所以長守富。”

translations.literal: "full yet not overflowing—thereby one long preserves wealth."
translations.idiomatic: be full yet never overflow, and you may long keep your wealth."

sentences.zh: 是知高危不可不慎，滿溢不可不持。

translations.literal: From this one knows that high peril must not go unheeded, and fullness overflowing must not go unguarded.
translations.idiomatic: Hence height and peril demand caution, and fullness demands restraint.

sentences.zh: 《易》曰：“君子終日乾乾，夕惕若厲，無咎。”

translations.literal: The Changes says, "The noble man is vigorous all day and at evening is wary as if in peril—no blame."
translations.idiomatic: The Book of Changes says, "The noble man strives all day and at evening is wary as if in danger—then he is without blame."

sentences.zh: 敬慎之謂也。

translations.literal: This is what is meant by reverence and caution.
translations.idiomatic: That is what reverence and caution mean.

sentences.zh: 在於凡庶，參守而行之，猶可以高振聲華，坐致榮祿。

translations.literal: Even among common people, if one practices and keeps to this, one may still raise one's fame and reputation high and attain honor and salary while seated.
translations.idiomatic: Even ordinary men who live by this may raise their renown and win rank and emolument.

sentences.zh: 況殿下有少陽之位，有天挺之姿，片善而天下必聞，小能而天下咸服，豈可不為盡善盡美之道，以取可大可久之名哉！

translations.literal: How much more does Your Highness hold the position of the lesser yang and possess heaven-endowed bearing—a single good deed and all under heaven must hear of it, a small ability and all under heaven surely submit—how can you fail to pursue the way of utmost goodness and beauty to obtain a name that may be great and long enduring!
translations.idiomatic: You hold the heir's place and heaven-given gifts: a single good act is heard throughout the realm, a small talent wins universal respect. How can you fail to pursue what is wholly good and beautiful and win a name that will endure?

sentences.zh: 伏願博覽經書以廣其德，屏退聲色以抑其情。

translations.literal: I venture to wish that you broadly read the classics to enlarge your virtue and dismiss music and women to restrain your passions.
translations.idiomatic: I beg you to read the classics widely and enlarge your virtue, and to put aside music and women and restrain your passions.

sentences.zh: 靜默無為，恬虛寡欲，非禮勿動，非法不言。

translations.literal: Be silent and without contrivance, tranquil and empty with few desires; do not move against ritual, do not speak against law.
translations.idiomatic: Be still and unforced, calm and sparing in desire; do nothing against ritual, speak nothing against law.

sentences.zh: 居處服玩，必循節儉；

translations.literal: In dwelling, dress, and playthings, you must follow frugality;
translations.idiomatic: In dwelling, dress, and ornaments, hold to frugality;

sentences.zh: 畋獵遊娛，不為縱逞。

translations.literal: in hunting, excursions, and diversions, do not give way to excess.
translations.idiomatic: in hunting and pastimes, do not give way to excess.

sentences.zh: 正人端士，必引而親之；

translations.literal: Upright men and proper scholars you must draw near and be intimate with;
translations.idiomatic: Draw upright men and proper scholars near you;

sentences.zh: 便僻側媚，必斥而遠之。

translations.literal: the facile, crooked, and fawning you must reject and keep at a distance.
translations.idiomatic: drive away the smooth, the crooked, and the fawning.

sentences.zh: 使惠聲溢於遠近，仁風翔於內外，則可以克享終吉，長保利貞，為上嗣之稱首，奉聖人之鴻業者矣。

translations.literal: If you cause beneficent fame to overflow near and far and humane winds to soar within and without, then you may attain enduring good fortune, long preserve profit and constancy, be foremost among heirs, and inherit the sage's great enterprise.
translations.idiomatic: Let your gracious name spread far and near and humane influence fill the realm within and without, and you may enjoy lasting good fortune, preserve profit and constancy, stand first among heirs, and inherit the sage sovereign's great enterprise.

sentences.zh: 又嚐為《諭善箴》以獻太子。

translations.literal: He also once composed an "Admonition on Goodness" and presented it to the crown prince.
translations.idiomatic: He also wrote an "Admonition on Goodness" and presented it to the crown prince.

sentences.zh: 太子善之，賜物甚厚。

translations.literal: The crown prince approved it and bestowed gifts in great abundance.
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince praised it and rewarded him generously.

sentences.zh: 承慶又以人之用心，多擾濁浮躁，罕詣衝和之境，乃著《靈台賦》以廣其誌，辭多不載。

translations.literal: Chengqing also held that people's minds are mostly disturbed, turbid, and restless, and rarely reach the realm of serene harmony; he therefore composed the "Rhapsody on the Spirit Terrace" to enlarge his intent—the text is mostly not recorded here.
translations.idiomatic: Chengqing also observed that men's minds are usually restless and turbid and rarely attain serene harmony; he wrote the "Rhapsody on the Spirit Terrace" to set forth his views, but most of the text is omitted here.

sentences.zh: 調露初，東宮廢，出為烏程令，風化大行。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tiaolu, the eastern palace was abolished; he was sent out as magistrate of Wucheng, and moral transformation was greatly carried out.
translations.idiomatic: When Tiaolu began, the crown prince was deposed; Chengqing was posted as magistrate of Wucheng, where he carried out a great moral transformation.

sentences.zh: 長壽中，累遷鳳閣舍人，兼掌天官選事。

translations.literal: During Changshou he was repeatedly promoted to attendant of the Fenige and concurrently managed selection affairs of the heaven office.
translations.idiomatic: During the Changshou era he rose to attendant of the Fenige and concurrently oversaw personnel selection in the Ministry of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 承慶屬文迅捷，雖軍國大事，下筆輒成，未嚐起草。

translations.literal: Chengqing composed with swift facility; even on great matters of army and state, when he put pen to paper it was at once complete—he never drafted a rough copy.
translations.idiomatic: Chengqing wrote with extraordinary speed; even on weighty matters of state, his compositions were finished at a stroke, and he never needed a draft.

sentences.zh: 尋坐忤大臣旨，出為沂州刺史。

translations.literal: Before long he was punished for going against senior ministers' intent and was sent out as prefect of Yi Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he offended the senior ministers and was posted out as prefect of Yi.

sentences.zh: 未幾，詔復舊職，依前掌天官選事。

translations.literal: Before long, by edict he was restored to his former post and, as before, managed selection affairs of the heaven office.
translations.idiomatic: Not long after, an edict restored him to his former office, and he again oversaw personnel selection in the Ministry of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 久之，以病免，改授太子諭德。

translations.literal: After some time, he was removed on account of illness and was reassigned as mentor to the crown prince.
translations.idiomatic: After some time illness forced his retirement, and he was reassigned as mentor to the crown prince.

sentences.zh: 後曆豫、虢等州刺史，頗著聲績，制書褒美。

translations.literal: Later he served in succession as prefect of Yu, Guo, and other prefectures, won considerable reputation and achievement, and received edicts of praise.
translations.idiomatic: He later served successively as prefect of Yu, Guo, and other prefectures, winning notable distinction, and received imperial commendations.

sentences.zh: 長安初，入為司仆少卿，轉天官侍郎，兼修國史。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Chang'an, he entered office as vice minister of the Court of the Imperial Stud and was transferred to vice minister of the heaven office, concurrently compiling the national history.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Chang'an era he was appointed vice minister of the Court of the Imperial Stud, then transferred to vice minister of the Ministry of Personnel while also serving as a compiler of the national history.

sentences.zh: 承慶自天授以來，三掌天官選事，銓授平允，海內稱之。

translations.literal: Since the Tianshou era Chengqing had three times managed selection affairs of the heaven office; his assessments and appointments were fair and equitable, and within the seas he was praised for it.
translations.idiomatic: From the Tianshou era onward Chengqing had thrice overseen personnel selection; his appointments were fair and impartial, and he was praised throughout the realm.

sentences.zh: 尋拜鳳閣侍郎、同鳳閣鸞台平章事，仍依舊兼修國史。

translations.literal: Before long he was appointed vice minister of the Fenige and associate counselor of equal rank with the Fenige and Luantai, and as before concurrently compiled the national history.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon made vice minister of the Fenige and associate chief minister, continuing to compile the national history as before.

sentences.zh: 神龍初，坐附推張易之弟昌宗失實，配流嶺表。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Shenlong, he was punished because, in supporting an impeachment, he had falsely implicated Zhang Yizhi's younger brother Changzong, and was banished to exile beyond the Ling mountains.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Shenlong era he was condemned for falsely implicating Zhang Changzong, Zhang Yizhi's younger brother, in an impeachment, and was exiled to the far south.

sentences.zh: 時易之等既伏誅，承慶去巾解帶而待罪。

translations.literal: At that time Yizhi and his associates had already been executed; Chengqing removed his cap and loosened his belt to await punishment.
translations.idiomatic: By then Zhang Yizhi and his faction had already been executed; Chengqing removed his cap and belt and waited to accept punishment.

sentences.zh: 時欲草赦書，眾議以為無如承慶者，乃召承慶為之。

translations.literal: At that time they wished to draft an amnesty edict; in general discussion none was thought equal to Chengqing, so Chengqing was summoned to compose it.
translations.idiomatic: When the court needed to draft an amnesty edict, everyone agreed no one could do it better than Chengqing, and he was summoned to write it.

sentences.zh: 承慶神色不撓，援筆而成，辭甚典美，當時鹹歎服之。

translations.literal: Chengqing's expression did not falter; he took up the brush and it was completed; the language was very classic and fine, and at the time all sighed in admiration.
translations.idiomatic: Chengqing showed not the slightest unease; he took up his brush and the draft was finished at once—elegant and polished—and all who witnessed it admired him.

sentences.zh: 歲餘，起授辰州刺史，未之任，入為秘書員外少監，兼修國史。

translations.literal: After more than a year he was recalled and appointed prefect of Chen Prefecture; before taking up the post he entered office as acting vice director of the Secretariat, concurrently compiling the national history.
translations.idiomatic: More than a year later he was recalled and appointed prefect of Chen, but before assuming the post he was made acting vice director of the Secretariat and again charged with compiling the national history.

sentences.zh: 尋以修《則天實錄》之功，賜爵扶陽縣子，賚物五百段。

translations.literal: Before long, for his work in compiling the Veritable Records of Zetian, he was granted the noble rank of Viscount of Fuyang County and awarded five hundred rolls of goods.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward, for compiling the Veritable Records of Empress Wu, he was ennobled as Viscount of Fuyang County and given five hundred rolls of goods.

sentences.zh: 又製撰《則天皇后紀聖文》，中宗稱善，特加銀青光祿大夫。

translations.literal: He also composed the "Commemorative Text on the Sagely Virtue of Empress Zetian"; Zhongzong praised it, and he was specially promoted to grand master with the silver seal and blue ribbon.
translations.idiomatic: He also composed the "Commemorative Text on the Sagely Virtue of Empress Zetian"; Zhongzong praised it and specially promoted him to Grand Master with the Silver Seal and Blue Ribbon.

sentences.zh: 俄授黃門侍郎，仍依舊兼修國史，未拜而卒。

translations.literal: Shortly he was appointed vice minister of the Huangmen, and as before concurrently compiled the national history; before he could assume the appointment he died.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon appointed vice minister of the Huangmen and was still compiling the national history, but he died before he could take up the new post.

sentences.zh: 中宗傷悼久之，乃召其弟相州刺史嗣立令赴葬事，仍拜黃門侍郎，令繼兄位，其見用如此。

translations.literal: Zhongzong mourned him deeply for a long time, then summoned his younger brother Silizhi, prefect of Xiang Prefecture, to come and attend to the funeral affairs, and still appointed him vice minister of the Huangmen, ordering him to succeed his elder brother's post—such was the extent to which he was valued.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongzong mourned him deeply, summoned his younger brother Silizhi, then prefect of Xiang, to oversee the funeral, and appointed him vice minister of the Huangmen to succeed his brother's office—such was the esteem in which the family was held.

sentences.zh: 贈秘書監，諡曰溫。

translations.literal: He was posthumously given the office of director of the Secretariat, and his posthumous title was Wen.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously made director of the Secretariat, with the posthumous epithet Wen.

sentences.zh: 子長裕，膳部員外郎。

translations.literal: His son Changyu was a staff officer in the Ministry of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: His son Changyu served as a staff officer in the Ministry of Rites.

sentences.zh: 嗣立，承慶異母弟也。

translations.literal: Silizhi was Chengqing's younger brother by a different mother.
translations.idiomatic: Silizhi was Chengqing's half-brother.

sentences.zh: 母王氏，遇承慶甚嚴，每有杖罰，嗣立必解衣請代，母不聽，輒私自杖，母察知之，漸加恩貸，議者比晉從王祥、王覽。

translations.literal: His mother, Lady Wang, was very strict toward Chengqing; whenever there was beating and punishment, Silizhi would always remove his clothes and ask to take the punishment in his place; when his mother did not consent, he would privately beat himself; when his mother detected this, she gradually showed greater kindness and lenience; commentators compared this to the Jin brothers Wang Xiang and Wang Lan.
translations.idiomatic: Their mother, Lady Wang, was very strict with Chengqing; whenever he was to be beaten, Silizhi would bare his back and beg to take the punishment in his stead. When she refused, he would beat himself in secret. Once she found out, she grew more lenient with Chengqing. Commentators likened the brothers to Wang Xiang and Wang Lan of Jin.

sentences.zh: 少舉進士，累補雙流令，政有殊績，為蜀中之最。

translations.literal: In youth he passed the jinshi examination; he was repeatedly appointed magistrate of Shuangliu, his governance had outstanding achievement, and he was foremost in Shu.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination in his youth, served successively as magistrate of Shuangliu with outstanding results, and ranked first among officials in Shu.

sentences.zh: 三遷萊蕪令。

translations.literal: After three promotions he became magistrate of Laiwu.
translations.idiomatic: After three promotions he was made magistrate of Laiwu.

sentences.zh: 會承慶自鳳閣舍人以疾去職，則天召嗣立謂曰：“卿父往日嚐謂朕曰‘臣有兩男忠孝，堪事陛下。

translations.literal: It happened that Chengqing had left office as attendant of the Fenige on account of illness; Zetian summoned Silizhi and said, "Your father once told Us, 'Your subject has two sons, loyal and filial, fit to serve Your Majesty.
translations.idiomatic: When Chengqing resigned as Fenige attendant on account of illness, Empress Wu summoned Silizhi and said, "Your father once told me, 'I have two sons, loyal and filial, fit to serve Your Majesty.'

sentences.zh: ’自卿兄弟效職，如卿父言。

translations.literal: ' Since you brothers have served in office, it has been as your father said.
translations.idiomatic: Since you and your brother have taken office, it has been just as your father said.

sentences.zh: 今授卿鳳閣舍人，令卿兄弟自相替代。”

translations.literal: Now We appoint you attendant of the Fenige, so that you brothers may alternately replace one another."
translations.idiomatic: I now appoint you Fenige attendant, so that you and your brother may take turns in the post."

sentences.zh: 即日遷鳳閣舍人。

translations.literal: That same day he was transferred to attendant of the Fenige.
translations.idiomatic: That same day he was promoted to Fenige attendant.

sentences.zh: 時學校頹廢，刑法濫酷，嗣立上疏諫曰：

translations.literal: At that time schools had fallen into decay and punishments were excessively cruel; Silizhi submitted a memorial remonstrating, saying:
translations.idiomatic: At that time schools had fallen into ruin and the law had grown cruel and excessive; Silizhi submitted a memorial of remonstrance, saying:

sentences.zh: 臣聞古先哲王立學官，掌教國子以六德、六行、六藝，三教備而人道畢矣。

translations.literal: Your subject has heard that the sage kings of antiquity established schools, charged with teaching the sons of the state the six virtues, six conduct, and six arts; when the three teachings were complete, the way of humanity was fulfilled.
translations.idiomatic: I have heard that the sage kings of antiquity established schools to teach the sons of the state the six virtues, six modes of conduct, and six arts; when these three teachings were complete, the full way of humanity was realized.

sentences.zh: 《禮記》曰：“化人成俗，必由學乎。”

translations.literal: The Book of Rites says, "To transform people and form custom, must it not be through learning?"
translations.idiomatic: The Book of Rites says, "To transform people and shape custom, one must begin with learning."

sentences.zh: 學之於人，其用蓋博。

translations.literal: Learning in relation to people—its uses are broadly extensive.
translations.idiomatic: Learning's uses for human beings are far-reaching indeed.

sentences.zh: 故立太學以教於國，設庠序以化於邑，王之諸子、卿大夫士之子及國之俊選皆造焉。

translations.literal: Therefore they established the Grand Academy to teach within the state and set up village schools to transform in the districts; the king's sons, the sons of ministers, grand masters, and servicemen, and the state's outstanding selections all came there.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore they established the Grand Academy to teach the realm and founded local schools to transform the districts; the king's sons, the sons of ministers and officials, and the state's most promising candidates all attended.

sentences.zh: 八歲入小學，十五入太學。

translations.literal: At eight they entered the primary school; at fifteen they entered the Grand Academy.
translations.idiomatic: At eight they entered primary school; at fifteen they entered the Grand Academy.

sentences.zh: 春秋教以《禮》、《樂》，冬夏教以《詩》、《書》。

translations.literal: In spring and autumn they were taught the Rites and Music; in winter and summer they were taught the Odes and Documents.
translations.idiomatic: In spring and autumn they were taught the Rites and Music; in winter and summer they were taught the Odes and Documents.

sentences.zh: 是以教洽而化流，行成而不悖。

translations.literal: Thus instruction was thorough and transformation flowed abroad; conduct was formed and did not deviate.
translations.idiomatic: Thus instruction reached everywhere and moral transformation spread; conduct was formed and did not stray from the right path.

sentences.zh: 自天子以至於庶人，未有不須學而成者也。

translations.literal: From the Son of Heaven down to the common people, there was none who did not need learning in order to be formed.
translations.idiomatic: From the Son of Heaven down to the common people, none could be fully formed without learning.

sentences.zh: 國家自永淳已來，二十餘載，國學廢散，胄子衰缺，時輕儒學之官，莫存章句之選。

translations.literal: Our state, since Yongchun, for more than twenty years, has seen the national academy abandoned and dispersed, the sons of officials in decline and shortage; the age has slighted the offices of Confucian learning, and none have preserved selection by textual commentary.
translations.idiomatic: For more than twenty years since the Yongchun era, the national academy has lain abandoned, its students dwindled and dispersed; the age has slighted Confucian learning, and no one any longer selects officials by mastery of the classics.

sentences.zh: 貴門後進，競以僥幸升班；

translations.literal: The younger scions of noble houses all competed to rise in rank by lucky chance;
translations.idiomatic: Young men from noble families competed to advance by sheer luck;

sentences.zh: 寒族常流，復因淩替弛業。

translations.literal: the ordinary streams of humble clans, moreover because of decline and neglect, let their studies lapse.
translations.idiomatic: while men from humble families, worn down by hardship, abandoned their studies altogether.

sentences.zh: 考試之際，秀茂罕登，驅之臨人，何以從政？

translations.literal: At the time of examinations, outstanding and flourishing talent rarely passed; if such men are driven to govern people, how can they conduct government?
translations.idiomatic: At examination time, outstanding talent rarely succeeds; if such men are sent out to govern, how can they administer affairs?

sentences.zh: 又垂拱之後，文明在辰，盛典鴻休，日書月至，因藉際會，入仕尤多。

translations.literal: Moreover, after Chuigong, when civilization was at its height, grand ceremonies and glorious felicities came day after day and month after month; by seizing the occasion, entry into office was especially numerous.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, after Chuigong, when the age was at its height of civilization, grand ceremonies and glorious blessings followed one after another, and many seized the moment to enter office.

sentences.zh: 加以讒邪凶黨來俊臣之屬，妄執威權，恣行枉陷，正直之伍，死亡為憂，道路以目，人無固誌，罕有執不撓之懷，殉至公之節，偷安苟免，聊以卒歲。

translations.literal: Added to this, the slanderous, wicked, and vicious faction—men like Lai Junchen—wantonly wielded awesome power and freely carried out false accusations; among upright men, death was a constant worry; on the roads people exchanged glances in fear; men had no steadfast resolve; rarely did anyone hold an unyielding heart or sacrifice himself for utmost public integrity; they sought safety and easy escape and merely passed the year.
translations.idiomatic: To this was added the slanderous and vicious faction led by Lai Junchen, who usurped power and freely framed the innocent; upright men lived in constant fear of death, people averted their eyes in the streets, and few held to unwavering integrity or sacrificed themselves for the public good—they merely sought safety and drifted through the year.

sentences.zh: 遂使綱領不振，請托公行，選舉之曹，彌長渝濫。

translations.literal: Thus the governing principles were not invigorated, patronage requests went openly about, and in the appointment offices corruption grew ever longer and more excessive.
translations.idiomatic: As a result governance slackened, patronage ran rampant, and the appointment offices grew ever more corrupt.

sentences.zh: 隨班少經術之士，攝職多庸瑣之才，徒以猛暴相誇，罕能清惠自勖。

translations.literal: Those advancing through the ranks had few men versed in the classics; those holding office were mostly petty and trivial talents, who boasted only of severity and violence and rarely could encourage themselves toward cleanness and kindness.
translations.idiomatic: Those advancing through the ranks had little knowledge of the classics, while those holding office were mostly petty mediocrities, boasting only of severity and violence and rarely striving for cleanness and kindness.

sentences.zh: 使海內黔首，騷然不安，州縣官僚，貪鄙未息，而望事必循理，俗致康寧，不可得也。

translations.literal: This caused the black-haired people within the seas to be restlessly unsettled, and prefectural and county officials' greed and baseness did not cease; yet to expect affairs necessarily to follow reason and customs to attain peace and tranquility—this cannot be obtained.
translations.idiomatic: This left the common people throughout the realm in restless turmoil, official greed unchecked, and made orderly governance and peaceful customs impossible.

sentences.zh: 陛下誠能下明製，發德音，廣開庠序，大敦學校，三館生徒，即令追集。

translations.literal: If Your Majesty can truly issue clear regulations, proclaim virtuous edicts, widely open village schools, greatly encourage the schools, and immediately order the students of the three halls to be recalled and gathered.
translations.idiomatic: If Your Majesty would issue clear edicts and proclaim benevolent decrees, widely reopen the schools, greatly revive learning, and immediately recall the students of the three halls,

sentences.zh: 王公已下子弟，不容別求仕進，皆入國學，服膺訓典。

translations.literal: The sons of princes and dukes downward must not be allowed to seek office advancement elsewhere; all must enter the national academy and cherish the canonical teachings.
translations.idiomatic: sons of princes and dukes must not seek office by other routes but must all enter the national academy and devote themselves to the canonical teachings.

sentences.zh: 崇飾館廟，尊尚儒師，盛陳奠菜之儀，宏敷講說之會，使士庶觀聽，有所發揚，弘獎道德，於是乎在。

translations.literal: Adorn and embellish the halls and temples, honor and esteem Confucian teachers, grandly display the rites of offering vegetables, and broadly hold assemblies for lecturing and exposition, so that scholars and commoners may observe and listen and be inspired to advance; to magnify and encourage virtue lies herein.
translations.idiomatic: Adorn the academies, honor Confucian teachers, hold solemn sacrificial ceremonies and grand lectures, and let scholars and commoners witness them and be inspired—thus moral cultivation would be greatly encouraged.

sentences.zh: 則四海之內，靡然向風，延頸舉足，鹹知所向。

translations.literal: Then within the four seas all would turn toward the wind, craning their necks and lifting their feet, all knowing where to go.
translations.idiomatic: Then throughout the realm all would turn toward virtue, every eye and every step knowing where to go.

sentences.zh: 然後審持衡鏡，妙擇良能，以之臨人，寄之調俗。

translations.literal: After that, carefully hold the scales and mirror, subtly select the capable and good, use them to govern people, and entrust to them the harmonizing of custom.
translations.idiomatic: Then carefully weigh merit and select the truly capable, appoint them to govern the people, and charge them with transforming local customs.

sentences.zh: 則官無侵暴之政，人有安樂之心，居人則相與樂業，百姓則皆戀桑梓，豈復憂其逃散而貧窶哉！

translations.literal: Then officials would have no oppressive and violent policies, and people would have hearts of peace and joy; those dwelling in place would together delight in their occupations, and the hundred surnames would all cherish their native districts—how could one again worry that they would flee and scatter and fall into poverty!
translations.idiomatic: Then officials would govern without oppression, and the people would live in contentment; residents would gladly pursue their occupations, and common folk would cherish their native places—who would then fear flight, dispersal, and poverty!

sentences.zh: 今天下戶口，亡逃過半，租調既減，國用不足。

translations.literal: Now under Heaven registered households—those who have fled and absconded exceed half; land tax and corvée levies having been reduced, state revenue is insufficient.
translations.idiomatic: Today more than half the registered households under Heaven have fled; tax revenues have fallen, and state funds are insufficient.

sentences.zh: 理人之急，尤切於茲。

translations.literal: The urgency of governing people is especially pressing here.
translations.idiomatic: The urgency of governing the people bears most pressingly on this point.

sentences.zh: 故知務學之源，豈唯潤身進德而已？

translations.literal: Thus one knows that the root of devoting oneself to learning—is it only to enrich the person and advance in virtue?
translations.idiomatic: Thus one sees that the root of learning is not merely to enrich oneself and advance in virtue—

sentences.zh: 將以誨人利國，可不務之哉！

translations.literal: It is also to instruct people and benefit the state—can one fail to devote oneself to it!
translations.idiomatic: it is also to instruct the people and benefit the state. How can it be neglected!

sentences.zh: 臣聞堯、舜之日，畫其衣冠；

translations.literal: Your subject has heard that in the days of Yao and Shun, they merely depicted offenders' clothing;
translations.idiomatic: I have heard that in the days of Yao and Shun, punishment amounted to no more than depicting the offenders' garb;

sentences.zh: 文、景之時，幾致刑措。

translations.literal: in the time of Wen and Jing, punishments were nearly set aside altogether.
translations.idiomatic: and in the reigns of Emperor Wen and Emperor Jing of Han, capital punishment was nearly abolished altogether.

sentences.zh: 曆茲千載，以為美談。

translations.literal: Through these thousand years they have been regarded as fine tales.
translations.idiomatic: For a thousand years these have been held up as shining examples.

sentences.zh: 臣伏惟陛下睿哲欽明，窮神知化，自軒、昊已降，莫之與京。

translations.literal: Your subject humbly considers that Your Majesty is wise, sagacious, reverent, and discerning, exhausting the spirit and knowing transformation; from Xuanyuan and Haohao downward, none can compare.
translations.idiomatic: I humbly consider that Your Majesty is wise, reverent, and discerning, penetrating the workings of spirit and transformation; since the sage kings Xuanyuan and Haohao, none has equaled you.

sentences.zh: 獨有往之論法，或未盡善，皆由主司奸凶，惑亂視聽。

translations.literal: Only in the discussion of law in times past, perhaps it was not wholly good—all because the chief officials were wicked and vicious and confused what was seen and heard.
translations.idiomatic: Only in the administration of law in times past was the practice perhaps not wholly good—and this was entirely because wicked officials in charge confused what reached your eyes and ears.

sentences.zh: 尋而陛下聖察，具詳之矣，然竟未能顯其本源，明其前事，令天下萬姓識陛下本心，尚使四海多銜冤之人，九泉有抱痛之鬼。

translations.literal: Before long Your Majesty's sage scrutiny fully examined it; yet in the end the root source was not made manifest, prior affairs were not clarified, and the myriad people under Heaven were not made to know Your Majesty's inner heart; still there are many in the four seas who harbor grievances, and in the nine springs there are ghosts who embrace pain.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty's sage scrutiny has since fully examined the matter, yet the root cause has still not been made clear nor past wrongs fully explained, so that the people under Heaven may know your true intent; many throughout the realm still harbor grievances, and in the realm below there are spirits who died in pain.

sentences.zh: 臣誠愚暗，不識大綱，請為陛下始末而言其事。

translations.literal: Your subject is truly dull and obscure and does not understand the great outline; I beg to speak of the matter for Your Majesty from beginning to end.
translations.idiomatic: I am truly dull and do not grasp the full scope of affairs, but I beg leave to set forth the matter for Your Majesty from beginning to end.

sentences.zh: 揚、豫之後，刑獄漸興，用法之伍，務於窮竟，連坐相牽，數年不絕。

translations.literal: After the Yang and Yu reign titles, criminal cases gradually arose; those who applied the law strove for exhaustive investigation, implicated one another by association, and for years it did not cease.
translations.idiomatic: After the Yang and Yu reign periods, criminal prosecutions gradually multiplied; those who applied the law strove to pursue cases to the end, implicating associates in endless chains that continued for years.

sentences.zh: 遂使巨奸大猾伺隙乘間，內苞豺狼之心，外示鷹鸇之跡，陰圖潛結，共相影會，構似是之言，成不赦之罪。

translations.literal: Thus great traitors and great schemers watched for gaps and seized intervals; inwardly they harbored the hearts of wolves, outwardly they displayed the tracks of hawks and falcons; secretly they plotted and covertly joined together, mutually echoing one another, fabricating seemingly plausible words and forming crimes that could not be pardoned.
translations.idiomatic: Thus great villains watched for openings; inwardly they harbored wolfish hearts while outwardly they showed the ferocity of hawks and falcons; they plotted in secret, colluded with one another, fabricated plausible accusations, and fashioned unpardonable crimes.

sentences.zh: 皆深為巧詆，恣行楚毒，人不勝痛，便乞自誣，公卿士庶，連頸受戮。

translations.literal: All deeply practiced crafty slander and freely carried out cruel torture; when people could not bear the pain, they would beg to confess falsely; ministers, officials, scholars, and commoners were linked by the neck and suffered execution.
translations.idiomatic: They practiced cunning slander and freely inflicted cruel torture; unable to bear the pain, victims begged to confess falsely; ministers, officials, and commoners alike were led to execution in chains.

sentences.zh: 道路籍籍，雖知非辜，而鍛練已成，辯占皆合。

translations.literal: On the roads there was widespread talk; although people knew the victims were not guilty, the forged evidence was already complete and the confessions and divinations all matched.
translations.idiomatic: Rumor spread along the roads; though people knew the accused were innocent, the fabricated evidence was complete and every confession and oracle matched.

sentences.zh: 縱皋陶為理，於公定刑，則謂汙宮毀柩，猶未塞責。

translations.literal: Even if Gao Yao were to judge the case and Yu Gong were to fix the punishment, it would be said that defiling the palace and destroying the coffin still did not satisfy the debt of responsibility.
translations.idiomatic: Even if Gao Yao himself were to judge the case and Yu Gong to fix the sentence, it would be said that defiling the palace and destroying the coffin still fell short of the debt owed.

sentences.zh: 雖陛下仁慈哀念，恤獄緩死，及覽辭狀，便已周密，皆謂勘鞫得情，是其實犯，雖欲寬舍，其如法何？

translations.literal: Although Your Majesty was benevolent and compassionate, pitying prisoners and deferring death, when you reviewed the written statements they were already thorough and complete; all said the investigation and interrogation had obtained the truth and that these were the actual crimes; even if you wished to show leniency, what could be done according to law?
translations.idiomatic: Though Your Majesty was benevolent and compassionate, pitying prisoners and deferring executions, when you reviewed the case records they appeared thorough and complete; all said the investigation had obtained the truth and the crimes were real—how could you show leniency when the law seemed to forbid it?

sentences.zh: 於是小乃身誅，大則族滅，相緣共坐者，不可勝言。

translations.literal: Thus in lesser cases there was execution of the person, in greater cases extermination of the clan; those implicated and jointly punished cannot be fully described.
translations.idiomatic: Thus in lesser cases the accused were executed, in greater cases entire clans were exterminated; those implicated and punished jointly are beyond counting.

sentences.zh: 此豈宿構仇嫌，將申報復，皆圖苟成功效，自求官賞。

translations.literal: Was this because of long-standing grudges they wished to avenge? All schemed merely to achieve results and sought office and reward for themselves.
translations.idiomatic: This was not born of old grudges seeking revenge; all schemed merely to achieve results and win office and reward for themselves.

sentences.zh: 當時稱傳，謂為羅織。

translations.literal: At the time it was spoken of and transmitted, and called "fabricated entanglement."
translations.idiomatic: At the time people called this practice "fabricated nets."

sentences.zh: 其中陷刑得罪者，雖有敏識通材，被告言者便遭枉抑，心徒痛其冤酷，口莫能以自明。

translations.literal: Among those who fell into punishment and guilt, although some had keen insight and comprehensive talent, once accused they immediately suffered wrongful suppression; in heart they only grieved at the injustice and cruelty, but by mouth they could not make themselves understood.
translations.idiomatic: Among those condemned, even men of keen insight and broad talent, once accused, immediately suffered wrongful suppression; they grieved at the injustice in their hearts but could not speak to clear themselves.

sentences.zh: 或受誅夷，或遭竄殛，並甘心引分，赴之如歸。

translations.literal: Some received execution and extermination, some suffered banishment and sudden death; all willingly accepted their allotted fate and went to it as if returning home.
translations.idiomatic: Some were executed, some banished or put to sudden death; all willingly accepted their fate and went to it as if returning home.

sentences.zh: 故知弄法徒文，傷人實甚。

translations.literal: Thus one knows that manipulating the law with empty words truly harms people greatly.
translations.idiomatic: Thus one sees that manipulating the law with empty formalities inflicts grave harm upon people.

sentences.zh: 賴陛下特回聖察，昭然詳究。

translations.literal: Thanks to Your Majesty's specially turning back sage scrutiny, it was clearly and thoroughly investigated.
translations.idiomatic: Thanks to Your Majesty's specially turning your sage scrutiny to the matter, the truth was clearly and thoroughly investigated.

sentences.zh: 周興、丘勣之類，弘義、俊臣之徒，皆相次伏誅，事暴遐邇，而朝野慶泰，若再睹陽和。

translations.literal: Men like Zhou Xing and Qiu Ji, and the followers of Hongyi and Junchen, were all in succession executed; the affair was exposed far and near, and court and countryside rejoiced in peace, as if again beholding the warm spring sun.
translations.idiomatic: Men like Zhou Xing and Qiu Ji, and the followers of Hongyi and Lai Junchen, were executed one after another; the affair was exposed far and wide, and court and countryside rejoiced as if beholding the warm spring sun again.

sentences.zh: 且如仁傑、元忠，俱罹枉陷，被勘鞫之際，亦皆已自誣。

translations.literal: Moreover, such men as Renjie and Yuanzhong both suffered wrongful entrapment; at the time of investigation and interrogation, they too had already falsely confessed.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, men such as Di Renjie and Yuan Zhong both suffered wrongful entrapment; under interrogation they too had already falsely confessed.

sentences.zh: 向非陛下至明，垂以省察，則菹醢之戮，已及其身，欲望輸忠聖代，安可復得！

translations.literal: If not for Your Majesty's utmost clarity and your extending examination and scrutiny, the punishment of being minced would already have reached their persons; to hope that they could devote loyalty to the sage age—how could that again be obtained!
translations.idiomatic: Had Your Majesty not been supremely discerning and extended your scrutiny, they would already have suffered execution by dismemberment; how then could they ever again devote loyal service to this sage age!

sentences.zh: 陛下擢而升之，各為良輔，國之棟幹，稱此二人。

translations.literal: Your Majesty raised and promoted them; each became a fine assistant, pillars of the state—of these two men it is said.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty raised and promoted them; each became a fine minister and a pillar of the state—such are these two men.

sentences.zh: 何乃前非而後是哉？

translations.literal: Why were they wrong before and right afterward?
translations.idiomatic: Why were they condemned before and vindicated afterward?

sentences.zh: 誠由枉陷與甄明爾。

translations.literal: Truly it was because of wrongful entrapment and discerning clarification.
translations.idiomatic: Truly it was because of wrongful entrapment on the one hand and discerning clarification on the other.

sentences.zh: 但恐往之得罪者多並此流，則向時之冤者其數甚眾。

translations.literal: But I fear that many of those who were condemned in the past belong to this same category; then the number of wronged persons in former times must be very great.
translations.idiomatic: But I fear that many of those condemned in the past belong to this same category; the number of wrongfully punished must then be very great indeed.

sentences.zh: 昔殺一孝婦，尚或降災。

translations.literal: In antiquity, when one filial woman was killed, disaster might still descend.
translations.idiomatic: In antiquity, the execution of even one filial woman could bring down calamity.

sentences.zh: 而濫者蓋多，寧無怨氣！

translations.literal: Yet those who were wrongly condemned were probably many—how could there be no resentful qi!
translations.idiomatic: Yet those wrongly condemned were surely many—how could there be no resentment!

sentences.zh: 怨氣上達則水旱所興，欲望歲登，不可得也。

translations.literal: When resentful qi reaches upward, flood and drought arise; to hope for abundant years—this cannot be obtained.
translations.idiomatic: When resentment reaches Heaven, flood and drought follow; to hope for abundant harvests is then impossible.

sentences.zh: 倘陛下弘天地之大德，施雷雨之深仁，歸罪於削刻之徒，降恩於枉濫之伍。

translations.literal: If Your Majesty would magnify the great virtue of Heaven and Earth and bestow the deep benevolence of thunder and rain, assign guilt to the harsh and cutting faction, and extend grace to the wrongly condemned multitude.
translations.idiomatic: If Your Majesty would magnify the great virtue of Heaven and Earth and bestow the deep benevolence of thunder and rain, assign guilt to the harsh persecutors, and extend grace to the wrongly condemned,

sentences.zh: 自垂拱已來，大辟罪已下，常赦所不原者，罪無輕重，一皆原洗，被以昭蘇。

translations.literal: From Chuigong onward, for capital crimes and below, even those normally excluded from ordinary amnesties—regardless of the weight of guilt—all would be pardoned and cleansed, and clothed in renewed life.
translations.idiomatic: from Chuigong onward, for capital crimes and below, even those normally excluded from ordinary amnesties—regardless of severity—all would be pardoned and restored to life.

sentences.zh: 伏法之輩，追還官爵，緣累之徒，普沾恩造。

translations.literal: Those who submitted to the law would have their offices and ranks restored; those implicated by association would universally receive the grace of creation.
translations.idiomatic: Those who suffered execution would have their offices and ranks restored, and those implicated by association would all share in your grace.

sentences.zh: 如此則天下知此所陷罪，元非陛下之意，鹹是虐吏之辜。

translations.literal: If it were thus, then under Heaven all would know that the crimes into which they were entrapped were originally not Your Majesty's intent, but entirely the guilt of cruel officials.
translations.idiomatic: Then all under Heaven would know that the crimes for which they were condemned were never Your Majesty's intent but entirely the fault of cruel officials.

sentences.zh: 幽明歡欣，則感通和氣；

translations.literal: When the hidden and the manifest rejoice together, then responsive communion with harmonious qi follows;
translations.idiomatic: When the living and the dead rejoice together, harmonious qi responds;

sentences.zh: 和氣下降，則風雨以時；

translations.literal: when harmonious qi descends, then wind and rain come in season;
translations.idiomatic: when harmonious qi descends, wind and rain come in season;

sentences.zh: 風雨以時，則五穀豐稔；

translations.literal: when wind and rain come in season, then the five grains are abundant;
translations.idiomatic: when wind and rain come in season, the five grains flourish;

sentences.zh: 歲既稔矣，人亦安矣。

translations.literal: when the year is abundant, people are also at peace.
translations.idiomatic: when harvests are abundant, the people are at peace.

sentences.zh: 太平之美，亦何遠哉！

translations.literal: The beauty of great peace—how far can it be!
translations.idiomatic: The beauty of great peace—how far off can it be!

sentences.zh: 伏願陛下深察。

translations.literal: Your subject humbly wishes that Your Majesty would deeply examine this.
translations.idiomatic: I humbly beg Your Majesty to consider this deeply.

sentences.zh: 尋遷秋官侍郎，三過鳳閣侍郎、同鳳閣鸞台平章事。

translations.literal: Before long he was transferred to vice minister of the autumn office; three times he passed through vice minister of the Fenige and associate counselor of equal rank with the Fenige and Luantai.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he was transferred to vice minister of the Ministry of Justice, and three times served as vice minister of the Fenige and associate chief minister.

sentences.zh: 長安中，則天嚐與宰臣議及州縣官吏，納言李嶠、夏官尚書唐休璟等奏曰：“臣等謬膺大任，不能使兵革止息，倉府殷盈，戶口尚有逋逃，官人未免貪濁，使陛下臨朝軫歎，屢以為言，夙夜慚惶，不知啟處。

translations.literal: During Chang'an, Zetian once discussed with chief ministers the officials of prefectures and counties; chief minister of the Left Li Qiao, minister of summer affairs Tang Xiujing, and others memorialized, saying, "Your subjects have wrongly received great responsibility; we cannot cause weapons and armor to cease, granaries and treasuries to be full, registered households still to have fugitives and absconders, or officials to be free from greed and corruption—so that Your Majesty at court sighs in concern and repeatedly speaks of it; morning and night we are ashamed and fearful, not knowing how to comport ourselves.
translations.idiomatic: During the Chang'an era, Empress Wu once discussed prefectural and county officials with her chief ministers; Chief Minister Li Qiao, Minister of War Tang Xiujing, and others memorialized, saying, "We have undeservedly received great responsibility yet cannot halt warfare, fill the granaries, stop the flight of registered households, or keep officials from greed and corruption—so that Your Majesty sighs at court and speaks of this repeatedly; day and night we are ashamed and do not know what to do.

sentences.zh: 伏思當今要務，莫過富國安人。

translations.literal: Your subjects humbly consider that among present urgent tasks, none surpass enriching the state and settling the people.
translations.idiomatic: We humbly consider that among the urgent tasks of the day, none surpass enriching the state and securing the people.

sentences.zh: 富國安人之方，在擇刺史。

translations.literal: The method of enriching the state and settling the people lies in selecting prefects.
translations.idiomatic: The way to enrich the state and secure the people lies in selecting good prefects.

sentences.zh: 竊見朝廷物議，莫不重內官，輕外職，每除授牧伯，皆再三披訴。

translations.literal: Your subjects have privately observed that in court public opinion, all value inner offices heavily and slight outer posts; whenever prefects are appointed and invested, all repeatedly plead and protest.
translations.idiomatic: We have observed that court opinion universally values capital appointments and slighted provincial posts; whenever a prefectural appointment is made, officials repeatedly plead and protest.

sentences.zh: 比來所遣外任，多是貶累之人，風俗不澄，實由於此。

translations.literal: Recently those sent out to outer appointments have mostly been men demoted and implicated; that customs are not clear and pure truly stems from this.
translations.idiomatic: Recently those sent to provincial posts have mostly been men under demotion or implicated in others' crimes; that local customs have not improved stems truly from this.

sentences.zh: 今望於台閣寺監，妙簡賢良，分典大州，共康庶績。

translations.literal: Now we hope at the Terrace Offices, Central Secretariat, Directorates, and Commissions finely to select the worthy and good, divide to administer great prefectures, and together bring peace to the myriad achievements.
translations.idiomatic: We ask that worthy men be carefully chosen from among the central ministries and directorates, assigned to govern major prefectures, and together restore good order throughout the realm.

sentences.zh: 臣等請輟近侍，率先具僚，務在憂國濟人，庶當有所補益。”

translations.literal: Your subjects request to relinquish close attendance, take the lead before all the officials, make it their task to worry for the state and succor the people, and perhaps thereby bring some benefit.
translations.idiomatic: We ask to leave our posts at court, take the lead among our colleagues, devote ourselves to serving the state and helping the people, and thereby bring some real benefit."

sentences.zh: 則天曰：“卿等處鸞台鳳閣，誰為此行？”

translations.literal: Wu Zetian said, "You serve at Luantai and Fengge — who will go on this mission?"
translations.idiomatic: Empress Wu said, "You hold office in the Secretariat — who among you will undertake this appointment?"

sentences.zh: 嗣立率先對曰：“臣以庸愚，謬膺獎擢，內掌機密，非臣所堪。

translations.literal: Sili was first to reply, saying, "Your subject, being mediocre and foolish, has wrongly received promotion and reward; holding confidential matters within, this is not what your subject can bear."
translations.idiomatic: Sili answered first: "I am a mediocre and unworthy man who was undeservedly promoted; I am not fit to handle state secrets at court.

sentences.zh: 承乏外台，庶當盡節，倘垂采錄，臣願此行。”

translations.literal: Accepting the vacancy at the outer commission, perhaps I should exhaust my loyalty; if Your Majesty would favorably take note, your subject wishes this journey.
translations.idiomatic: If I may fill a provincial post, I will do my utmost; should Your Majesty approve, I am willing to go."

sentences.zh: 於是嗣立帶本官檢校汴州刺史。

translations.literal: Thereupon Sili retained his original office and was made Acting Prefect of Bianzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Sili was then appointed acting Prefect of Bianzhou while retaining his existing rank.

sentences.zh: 無幾，嗣立兄承慶入知政事，嗣立轉成均祭酒，兼檢校魏州刺史。

translations.literal: Before long, Sili's elder brother Chengqing entered to manage state affairs; Sili was transferred to Superintendent of Chengjun and concurrently Acting Prefect of Weizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward Sili's elder brother Chengqing entered the chief council; Sili became Superintendent of the Directorate of Education and acting Prefect of Weizhou.

sentences.zh: 又徙洺州刺史。

translations.literal: He was again moved to Prefect of Mingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was later transferred to Prefect of Mingzhou.

sentences.zh: 尋坐承慶左授饒州長史。

translations.literal: Before long, implicated by Chengqing, he was demoted and appointed Senior Administrator of Raozhou.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was demoted because of Chengqing's fall and appointed Senior Administrator of Raozhou.

sentences.zh: 歲餘，徵為太仆少卿，兼掌吏部選事。

translations.literal: After a year and more, he was summoned as Vice Minister of the Stud and concurrently managed selection affairs in the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: After more than a year he was recalled as Vice Minister of the Stud and put in charge of personnel selection at the Ministry of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 神龍二年，為相州刺史。

translations.literal: In the second year of Shenlong, he became Prefect of Xiangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In 706 he was appointed Prefect of Xiangzhou.

sentences.zh: 及承慶卒，代為黃門侍郎，轉太府卿，加修文館學士。

translations.literal: When Chengqing died, he replaced him as Vice Minister of the Chancellery, was transferred to Minister of the Court of the Imperial Treasury, and given the added title Scholar of the Xiuxuan Pavilion.
translations.idiomatic: When Chengqing died, he succeeded him as Vice Minister of the Chancellery, then became Minister of the Court of the Imperial Treasury and was made a Scholar of the Xiuxuan Pavilion.

sentences.zh: 景龍三年，轉兵部尚書、同中書門下三品。

translations.literal: In the third year of Jinglong, he was transferred to Minister of War and Associate Grand Counselor of the Chancellery and Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: In 709 he was made Minister of War and appointed Associate Grand Counselor.

sentences.zh: 時中宗崇飾寺觀，又濫食封邑者眾，國用虛竭。

translations.literal: At that time Emperor Zhongzong lavishly adorned temples and monasteries, and many also indiscriminately received fief income from households; state expenditures were emptied and exhausted.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Emperor Zhongzong lavishly decorated temples and monasteries, fief incomes were granted indiscriminately, and the treasury was drained dry.

sentences.zh: 嗣立上疏諫曰：

translations.literal: Sili submitted a memorial remonstrating, saying:
translations.idiomatic: Sili submitted a memorial of remonstrance, saying:

sentences.zh: 臣聞國無九年之儲，家無三年之蓄，家非其家，國非其國。

translations.literal: Your subject has heard that when a state lacks nine years' stores and a household lacks three years' savings, the household is not truly a household and the state is not truly a state.
translations.idiomatic: I have heard it said that when a state has no nine years' reserves and a household no three years' savings, neither household nor state can endure.

sentences.zh: 故知立國立家，皆資於儲蓄矣。

translations.literal: Thus one knows that establishing a state and establishing a household both rely on accumulation and storage.
translations.idiomatic: This shows that both states and households depend upon reserves.

sentences.zh: 夫水旱之災，關之陰陽運數，非人智力所能及也。

translations.literal: As for flood and drought disasters, they concern the yin and yang and the cycle of fate; they are not within human wit and strength to reach.
translations.idiomatic: Floods and droughts belong to the workings of yin and yang and the cycles of fate, beyond what human wisdom can control.

sentences.zh: 堯遭大水，湯遭大旱，則知仁聖之君所不能免，當此時不至於困弊者，積也。

translations.literal: Yao encountered great flood and Tang encountered great drought — thus one knows that even benevolent and sage rulers cannot escape them; that in such times one does not reach distress and exhaustion is due to accumulation.
translations.idiomatic: Yao suffered great floods and Tang a severe drought — even sage rulers cannot escape such calamities; that they did not collapse in those times was because they had built up reserves.

sentences.zh: 今陛下倉庫之內，比稍空竭，尋常用度，不支一年。

translations.literal: Now within Your Majesty's granaries and storehouses, compared with before they are somewhat empty and exhausted; ordinary daily expenditures will not last a year.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty's granaries and treasuries are nearly empty; ordinary expenditures will not suffice for even a year.

sentences.zh: 倘有水旱，人須賑給，徵發時動，兵要資裝，則將何以備之？

translations.literal: If there are flood or drought, people will need relief and supply; when levies and deployments arise in season, armies need outfitting and stores — with what will you prepare for these?
translations.idiomatic: If flood or drought strikes, people must be fed; when levies and campaigns are called, armies must be equipped — how will you meet these needs?

sentences.zh: 其緣倉庫不實，妨於政化者，觸類而是。

translations.literal: Those matters where empty granaries and storehouses obstruct government and transformation — by type and kind all are so.
translations.idiomatic: Every kind of harm to good governance that stems from empty treasuries applies here.

sentences.zh: 臣竊見比者營造寺觀，其數極多，皆務取宏博，競崇環麗。

translations.literal: Your subject has privately seen that recently in constructing temples and monasteries, their number is extremely great; all strive to make them vast and broad, competing to exalt their splendor and beauty.
translations.idiomatic: I observe that temple and monastery construction has proliferated lately, each project striving for grandeur and competing in splendor.

sentences.zh: 大則費耗百十萬，小則尚用三五萬餘，略計都用資財，動至千萬已上。

translations.literal: Large ones consume one to two million; small ones still use thirty to fifty thousand and more; roughly estimating total resources used, each often reaches ten million and above.
translations.idiomatic: Large projects cost a million or more; even small ones run to thirty or fifty thousand — altogether, expenditures easily exceed ten million.

sentences.zh: 轉運木石，人牛不停，廢人功，害農務，事既非急，時多怨谘。

translations.literal: Transporting timber and stone, men and oxen without rest — human labor wasted, farming harmed; the affair is not urgent, yet at the time many complain and resent.
translations.idiomatic: Timber and stone are hauled without cease, wasting labor and harming agriculture — all for projects that are not urgent, yet provoking widespread resentment.

sentences.zh: 故《書》曰：“不作無益害有益，功乃成；

translations.literal: Therefore the Documents says, "Do not do what is useless and harm what is useful — then achievement is completed;
translations.idiomatic: Thus the Book of Documents says: "Do nothing useless that would harm what is useful, and your work will succeed;

sentences.zh: 不貴異物賤用物，民乃足。”

translations.literal: Do not value strange things and treat useful things cheaply — then the people will be sufficient.
translations.idiomatic: Do not prize exotic things and neglect what is useful, and the people will have enough."

sentences.zh: 誠哉此言，非虛談也。

translations.literal: Truly this saying — it is not empty talk.
translations.idiomatic: These words are true, not idle talk.

sentences.zh: 且玄旨秘妙，歸於空寂，苟非修心定慧，諸法皆涉有為。
