translations.literal: Moreover, the profound purport, secret and wondrous, returns to emptiness and stillness; if one does not cultivate the mind in concentration and wisdom, all dharmas involve conditioned effort.
translations.idiomatic: The deepest teachings of the Way return to emptiness and stillness; unless one cultivates the mind through meditation and wisdom, all religious practices remain mere worldly exertion.

sentences.zh: 至如土木雕刻等功，唯是殫竭人力，但學相誇壯麗，豈關降伏身心。

translations.literal: As for works of earth, wood, carving, and the like, they only exhaust human strength, merely teach one another to boast of magnificence — how does this relate to subduing body and mind?
translations.idiomatic: Building in earth and wood, carving and ornament — these only exhaust labor and teach rivals to outdo one another in grandeur; they have nothing to do with mastering the self.

sentences.zh: 且凡所興功，皆須掘鑿，蟄蟲在土，種類實多。

translations.literal: Moreover, every undertaking of works requires digging and hewing; dormant insects in the soil, their kinds are truly many.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, every construction project requires digging, and countless kinds of creatures lie dormant in the earth.

sentences.zh: 每日殺傷，動盈萬計，連年如此，損害可知。

translations.literal: Daily killing and injury, often filling tens of thousands — year after year thus, the harm can be known.
translations.idiomatic: Each day tens of thousands are killed; continued year after year, the damage is obvious.

sentences.zh: 聖人慈悲為心，豈有須行此事，不然之理，皎在目前。

translations.literal: The sage takes compassion as his heart — how could there be need to perform such things? That it is not so — the principle is bright before the eyes.
translations.idiomatic: The sage's heart is compassion — surely there is no reason to do such things; that this is wrong is plain for all to see.

sentences.zh: 世俗眾僧，未通其旨，不慮府庫空竭，不思聖人憂勞，謂廣樹福田，即是增修法教。

translations.literal: Worldly monks en masse have not penetrated its purport; they do not consider the emptying of the treasury, do not think of the sage's worry and toil, and say that broadly planting fields of merit is precisely increasing and cultivating the dharma teaching.
translations.idiomatic: Ordinary monks, failing to grasp this teaching, never worry about empty treasuries or the ruler's burdens — they believe that building more temples is itself deepening the faith.

sentences.zh: 倘水旱為災，人至饑餒，夷狄作梗，兵無資糧，陛下雖有龍象如雲，伽藍概日，豈能裨萬分之一，救元元之苦哉！

translations.literal: If flood and drought become disaster, people reach hunger and starvation, barbarians make obstruction, armies lack funds and grain — though Your Majesty has dragon-elephants like clouds and monasteries covering the sun, how could they aid one part in ten thousand and save the suffering of the myriad masses!
translations.idiomatic: If flood and drought bring famine, barbarians raid, and armies lack provisions — though you had monks as countless as clouds and monasteries blotting out the sun, could they relieve one ten-thousandth of the people's suffering?

sentences.zh: 於道法既有乖，在生人極為損，陛下豈可不深思之！

translations.literal: In the dao and dharma it already deviates; for the living people it is extremely harmful — how can Your Majesty not deeply consider this!
translations.idiomatic: This deviates from the true Way and deeply harms the living — Your Majesty must weigh this carefully!

sentences.zh: 臣竊見食封之家，其數甚眾。

translations.literal: Your subject has privately seen that households receiving fief income, their number is very great.
translations.idiomatic: I observe that the number of fief-holding households has grown very large.

sentences.zh: 昨略問戶部，雲用六十餘萬丁，一丁兩匹，即是一百二十萬已上。

translations.literal: Yesterday briefly questioning the Ministry of Revenue, they said six hundred-odd thousand able-bodied men are used; one man two bolts of silk — that is one million two hundred thousand and above.
translations.idiomatic: I recently asked the Ministry of Revenue: they reported over six hundred thousand able-bodied men levied, at two bolts of silk per man — more than 1.2 million bolts in all.

sentences.zh: 臣頃在太府，知每年庸調絹數，多不過百萬，少則七八十萬已來，比諸封家，所入全少。

translations.literal: Your subject recently was in the Court of the Imperial Treasury and knew that each year the bolts of silk from labor and land tax, at most not exceeding one million, at least seventy or eighty thousand — compared with fief households, what enters is entirely less.
translations.idiomatic: When I served at the Court of the Imperial Treasury, I knew that annual revenue from labor and land taxes totaled at most a million bolts, sometimes only seventy or eighty thousand — far less than what fief holders receive.

sentences.zh: 倘有蟲霜旱澇，曾不半在，國家支供，何以取給？

translations.literal: If there are insect damage, frost, drought, and waterlogging, not even half remains — state disbursements and supplies, with what will they be obtained?
translations.idiomatic: If insects, frost, drought, or flood cut the harvest by half, how will the state meet its obligations?

sentences.zh: 臣聞自封茅土，裂山河，皆須業著經綸，功申草昧，然後配宗廟之享，承帶礪之恩。

translations.literal: Your subject has heard that from the bestowing of fief lands and the carving of mountains and rivers, all must have achievements manifest in ordering the realm and merit declared in the founding age, and only then match enjoyment at the ancestral temple and receive the grace of the girdle and whetstone covenant.
translations.idiomatic: I have heard that fiefs and territorial grants are given only to those whose achievements in ordering the realm were proven at the dynasty's founding — and only then do they receive ancestral temple honors and the covenant of the girdle and whetstone.

sentences.zh: 皇運之初，功臣共定天下，當時食封才上三二十家，今以尋常特恩，遂至百家已上。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the imperial fortune, meritorious ministers together settled the realm; at that time those receiving fief income were only upward of twenty or thirty households; now through ordinary special grace, they have reached one hundred households and more.
translations.idiomatic: When the dynasty was founded, meritorious ministers together won the realm — only twenty or thirty families held fiefs; now, through routine special favors, their number exceeds a hundred.

sentences.zh: 國家租賦，太半私門，私門則資用有餘，國家則支計不足。

translations.literal: The state's land tax and levies — more than half go to private gates; private gates then have surplus in resources and use, the state then has insufficient disbursements and accounts.
translations.idiomatic: More than half the state's tax revenue now goes to private households, leaving them abundantly supplied while the government falls short.

sentences.zh: 有餘則或致奢侈，不足則坐致憂危，製國之方，豈謂為得？

translations.literal: When there is surplus some lead to extravagance; when there is insufficiency one sits and brings worry and peril — the method of governing the state, can it be called correct?
translations.idiomatic: Surplus breeds extravagance; shortfall brings crisis — is this a sound way to govern?

sentences.zh: 封戶之物，諸家自徵，或是官典，或是奴仆，多挾勢騁威，淩突州縣。

translations.literal: As for goods from fief households, each family collects them itself — some are official clerks, some are slaves and servants; many rely on power and unleash authority, encroaching upon and violating prefectures and counties.
translations.idiomatic: Fief income is collected by each household itself — by agents or by servants — who often abuse their power and bully local officials.

sentences.zh: 凡是封戶，不勝侵擾，或輸物多索裹頭，或相知要取中物，百姓怨歎，遠近共知。

translations.literal: All fief households, unable to bear the encroachment and harassment — sometimes when delivering goods they demand extra wrapping fees, sometimes acquaintances demand middle goods; the people complain and sigh, near and far all know.
translations.idiomatic: Fief households suffer constant harassment — inflated delivery charges, kickbacks demanded by intermediaries — and the people's grievances are known everywhere.

sentences.zh: 復有因將貨易，轉更生釁，徵打紛紛，曾不寧息，貧乏百姓，何以克堪！

translations.literal: Further, because of transporting goods for trade, quarrels arise anew; collection and beating in confusion, never at peace — impoverished common people, how can they bear it!
translations.idiomatic: Trade disputes lead to new violence; constant seizures and beatings never cease — how can poor common people endure it?

sentences.zh: 若必限丁物送太府，封家但於左藏請受，不得輒自征催，則必免侵擾，人冀蘇息。

translations.literal: If it must be fixed that per-capita goods be sent to the Court of the Imperial Treasury, fief households need only request receipt at the Left Treasury and may not on their own collect and press — then encroachment and harassment will surely be avoided, and people may hope to revive and rest.
translations.idiomatic: If tribute per household were sent directly to the treasury and fief holders drew their share from the Left Treasury without collecting it themselves, harassment would cease and the people could recover.

sentences.zh: 臣又聞設官分職，量事置吏，此本於理人而務安之也。

translations.literal: Your subject has further heard that establishing offices and dividing duties, gauging affairs to place clerks — this originally stems from governing people and making their task to secure them.
translations.idiomatic: I have also heard that offices are established and officials assigned according to need — the whole purpose is to govern the people and keep them secure.

sentences.zh: 故《書》曰“ 在官人，在安人。

translations.literal: Therefore the Documents says, "In employing men for office, in securing the people."
translations.idiomatic: Thus the Book of Documents says: "In appointing officials, in securing the people.

sentences.zh: 官人則哲，安人則惠。

translations.literal: Employing men for office, then discerning; securing the people, then benevolent.
translations.idiomatic: Choose wise men for office, and govern the people with kindness.

sentences.zh: 能哲而惠，何憂乎歡兜，何畏乎有苗”者也！

translations.literal: Able to be discerning and benevolent — what worry about Huan Dou, what fear of You Miao!" — such is the meaning!
translations.idiomatic: With wisdom and kindness combined, what need to fear Huan Dou or dread the Miao?" — so it runs!

sentences.zh: 是明官得其人，而天下自理矣。

translations.literal: This clarifies that when offices get their men, the realm under Heaven governs itself.
translations.idiomatic: This shows that when the right men hold office, the realm governs itself.

sentences.zh: 古者取人，必先采鄉曲之譽，然後辟於州郡；

translations.literal: In antiquity when taking men, one first gathered village and neighborhood reputation, then recruited them in prefectures and commanderies;
translations.idiomatic: In antiquity, officials were chosen first for local reputation, then summoned to serve in the prefectures;

sentences.zh: 州郡有聲，然後辟於五府；

translations.literal: when they had renown in prefectures and commanderies, then recruited them in the Five Offices;
translations.idiomatic: those who distinguished themselves there were recruited to the central ministries;

sentences.zh: 才著五府，然後升之天朝。

translations.literal: when talent was manifest in the Five Offices, then promoted them to the heavenly court.
translations.idiomatic: only after proving themselves at court were they promoted to the capital.

sentences.zh: 此則用一人所擇者甚悉，擢一士所曆者甚深。

translations.literal: This then — in using one man the choosing is very thorough, in elevating one scholar the course passed through is very deep.
translations.idiomatic: Thus the selection of a single official was exhaustive, and the testing of a single candidate was thorough.

sentences.zh: 孔子曰：“譬有美錦，不可使人學製。”

translations.literal: Confucius said, "Suppose there is fine brocade — one must not have people learn to make it."
translations.idiomatic: Confucius said: "Fine brocade should not be put into the hands of an untrained craftsman."

sentences.zh: 此明用人不可不審擇也。

translations.literal: This clarifies that employing men cannot but be carefully chosen.
translations.idiomatic: This shows that appointments must be made with the greatest care.

sentences.zh: 用得其才則理，非其才則亂，理亂所設，焉可不深擇之哉！

translations.literal: Use and get their talent then order; not their talent then disorder — order and disorder depend on what is established — how can one not deeply choose!
translations.idiomatic: The right talent brings order; the wrong man brings chaos — how can appointment not be made with utmost care?

sentences.zh: 今之取人，有異此道。

translations.literal: Today's taking of men differs from this way.
translations.idiomatic: Today's appointments follow a different path entirely.

sentences.zh: 多未甚試效，即頓至遷擢。

translations.literal: Many have not been much tested in effectiveness, yet suddenly reach transfer and promotion.
translations.idiomatic: Many are promoted abruptly without having been adequately tested.

sentences.zh: 夫趨競者人之常情，僥幸人之所趣。

translations.literal: Now striving and competing is the common disposition of people; luck-seeking is what people pursue.
translations.idiomatic: Ambition is human nature, and luck-seeking is what all pursue.

sentences.zh: 而今務進不避僥幸者，接踵比肩，布於文武之列。

translations.literal: Yet today those striving for advancement and not shunning luck-seeking follow heel to shoulder, range shoulder to shoulder, spread through civil and military ranks.
translations.idiomatic: Today those who scramble for advancement by any means crowd the civil and military ranks.

sentences.zh: 有文者用理內外，則有回邪贓汙上下敗亂之憂；

translations.literal: Those with civil skills used to govern inner and outer — then there is worry of crooked wickedness, filth and corruption, upper and lower defeated in disorder;
translations.idiomatic: Put unworthy literati in charge of governance, and corruption and disorder follow;

sentences.zh: 有武者用將軍戎，則有庸懦怯弱師旅喪亡之患。

translations.literal: Those with martial skills used to command armies and military affairs — then there is peril of mediocre, cowardly, weak, fearful armies lost and perished.
translations.idiomatic: Put unworthy warriors in command of armies, and troops will be routed through incompetence and cowardice.

sentences.zh: 補授無限，員闕不供，遂至員外置官，數倍正闕。

translations.literal: Supplementary appointments without limit, regular posts not supplied — thus reaching extra-establishment placement of officials, several times the regular vacancies.
translations.idiomatic: Appointments know no limit while regular posts go unfilled — supernumerary officials now outnumber authorized posts several times over.

sentences.zh: 曹署典吏，困於祗承，府庫倉儲，竭於資奉。

translations.literal: Bureau offices and chief clerks, trapped in reverent attendance; treasury granaries and stores, exhausted in supporting and supplying.
translations.idiomatic: Bureau staffs are overwhelmed with ceremonial obligations, and treasuries drained by salaries.

sentences.zh: 國家大事，豈甚於此！

translations.literal: The great affairs of the state — can anything be graver than this!
translations.idiomatic: Could any matter be more urgent for the state than this!

sentences.zh: 古者懸爵待士，唯有才者得之，若任用無才，則有才之路塞，賢人君子所以遁跡銷聲，常懷歎恨者也。

translations.literal: In antiquity ranks and titles were hung up awaiting scholars — only those with talent obtained them; if the talentless are employed, then the path for the talented is blocked — this is why worthy men and gentlemen hide their traces and silence their voices, always harboring sighs and regret.
translations.idiomatic: In antiquity offices awaited the worthy — only men of talent received them. When the unworthy are appointed, the talented are shut out; that is why worthy men withdraw from public life, nursing their grievances in silence.

sentences.zh: 且賢人君子，守於正直之道，遠於僥幸之門，若僥幸開，則賢者不可復出矣。

translations.literal: Moreover, worthy men and gentlemen keep to the upright way and keep far from the gate of luck-seeking; if luck-seeking is opened, then the worthy cannot emerge again.
translations.idiomatic: Worthy men hold to integrity and shun the path of favor-seeking; once favor-seeking is opened wide, the worthy will not come forward again.

sentences.zh: 賢者遂退，若欲求人安化洽，復不可得也。

translations.literal: The worthy then withdraw; if one seeks people's security and transformation harmonized, again it cannot be obtained.
translations.idiomatic: Once the worthy withdraw, you cannot hope to secure the people and bring harmony to the realm.

sentences.zh: 人若不安，國將危矣，陛下安可不深慮之！

translations.literal: If people are not secure, the state will be in peril — how can Your Majesty not deeply consider this!
translations.idiomatic: When the people are insecure, the state is in danger — Your Majesty must weigh this carefully!

sentences.zh: 又刺史、縣令，理人之首。

translations.literal: Moreover, prefects and magistrates are the head of governing people.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, prefects and magistrates are the foremost officials in governing the people.

sentences.zh: 近年已來，不存簡擇。

translations.literal: In recent years until now, there has been no careful selection.
translations.idiomatic: In recent years no care has been taken in selecting them.

sentences.zh: 京官有犯及聲望下者，方遣牧州；

translations.literal: Capital officials who have offenses or whose renown is low — only then are they dispatched to govern prefectures;
translations.idiomatic: Only capital officials who have committed offenses or whose reputation is poor are sent out as prefects;

sentences.zh: 吏部選人，暮年無手筆者，方擬縣令。

translations.literal: Ministry of Personnel selection candidates, in their declining years without brush and document skills — only then are they slated for magistrate.
translations.idiomatic: Only Ministry of Personnel candidates who are aging and untalented are slated for county magistrate.

sentences.zh: 此風久扇，上下同知，將此理人，何以率化？

translations.literal: This wind has long been blown, upper and lower all know it — using such men to govern people, with what will one lead and transform?
translations.idiomatic: This practice has long been known at every level — how can such men lead and transform the people?

sentences.zh: 今歲非豐稔，戶口流亡，國用空虛，租調減削。

translations.literal: This year is not abundant harvest; household registers flee and scatter; state use is empty and void; land and labor levies reduced and cut.
translations.idiomatic: This has not been a plentiful year; population is fleeing; the treasury is empty; tax revenues are shrinking.

sentences.zh: 陛下不以此留念，將何以理國乎？

translations.literal: Your Majesty not taking this to heart and considering — with what will you govern the state?
translations.idiomatic: If Your Majesty does not heed these matters, how will you govern the realm?

sentences.zh: 臣望下明製，具論前事，使有司改換簡擇，天下刺史、縣令，皆取才能有稱望者充。

translations.literal: Your subject hopes Your Majesty will issue clear regulations, fully discuss the foregoing matters, have the responsible offices change and carefully select — throughout the realm prefects and magistrates all take those with talent and reputation to fill the posts.
translations.idiomatic: I ask that Your Majesty issue clear orders, review these matters in full, and require that prefects and magistrates throughout the realm be chosen from among men of proven talent and reputation.

sentences.zh: 自今已往，應有遷除諸曹侍郎、兩省、兩台及五品已上清望官，先於刺史、縣令中選用。

translations.literal: From today forward, for all transfers and appointments to vice ministers of the various bureaus, the Two Departments, the Two Commissions, and pure-reputation offices of fifth rank and above — first select and employ from among prefects and magistrates.
translations.idiomatic: Henceforth, whenever appointing vice ministers, officials of the Two Departments and Two Commissions, or prestigious fifth-rank posts and above, choose first from among serving prefects and magistrates.

sentences.zh: 牧宰得人，天下大理，萬姓欣欣然，豈非太平樂事哉！

translations.literal: Prefects and magistrates get their men, the realm under Heaven is greatly ordered, the myriad people rejoice joyfully — is this not the happy affair of great peace!
translations.idiomatic: With the right men governing the provinces, the realm would be well ordered and the people glad — would that not be the joy of true peace!

sentences.zh: 唯陛下詳擇。

translations.literal: Only Your Majesty, carefully choose.
translations.idiomatic: I ask only that Your Majesty choose with care.

sentences.zh: 疏奏不納。

translations.literal: The memorial was submitted and not accepted.
translations.idiomatic: The memorial was rejected.

sentences.zh: 嗣立與韋庶人宗屬疏遠，中宗特令編入屬籍，由是顧賞尤重。

translations.literal: Sili was distantly related to Consort Wei by clan; Emperor Zhongzong specially ordered him entered in the clan register — thereby his favor and reward were especially heavy.
translations.idiomatic: Sili was only distantly related to Consort Wei, but Emperor Zhongzong specially enrolled him in the clan register, and thereafter favored him with exceptional generosity.

sentences.zh: 賞於驪山構營別業，中宗親往幸焉，自製詩序，令從官賦詩，賜絹二千匹。

translations.literal: Rewarded with construction of a separate estate at Mount Li, Emperor Zhongzong personally went to visit it, himself composed a preface to poems, ordered attending officials to compose poems, and bestowed two thousand bolts of silk.
translations.idiomatic: He was rewarded with an estate built for him at Mount Li; Emperor Zhongzong visited in person, wrote a preface to the occasion, had his officials compose poems, and granted two thousand bolts of silk.

sentences.zh: 因封嗣立為逍遙公，名其所居為清虛原幽棲穀。

translations.literal: Thereupon Sili was enfeoffed as Duke of Xiaoyao, and his residence was named Qingxu Plain and Youqi Valley.
translations.idiomatic: Sili was enfeoffed as Duke of Unfettered Ease, and his estate was named the Plain of Pure Emptiness and the Valley of Secluded Dwelling.

sentences.zh: 韋氏敗，幾為亂兵所害，寧王憲以嗣立是從母之夫，救護免之。

translations.literal: When the Wei clan fell, he nearly was harmed by mutinous troops; Prince of Ning Xian, because Sili was the husband of his mother's younger sister, rescued and protected him and spared him.
translations.idiomatic: When the Wei faction fell, he nearly perished at the hands of mutinous soldiers; Prince Xian of Ning, recognizing that Sili was husband to his maternal aunt, rescued him and saved his life.

sentences.zh: 睿宗踐祚，拜中書令。

translations.literal: When Emperor Ruizong ascended the throne, he was appointed Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Ruizong took the throne, Sili was appointed Director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 尋日，出為許州刺史。

translations.literal: Before long, he was sent out as Prefect of Xuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he was posted out as Prefect of Xuzhou.

sentences.zh: 以定冊尊立睿宗之功，賜實封一百戶。

translations.literal: For the merit of settling the succession and honoring and establishing Emperor Ruizong, he was granted one hundred households of actual fief income.
translations.idiomatic: For his role in securing the succession and enthroning Emperor Ruizong, he was granted a fief of one hundred actual households.

sentences.zh: 開元初，入為國子祭酒。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Kaiyuan, he entered the capital as Chancellor of the Directorate of Education.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of the Kaiyuan era he was recalled as Chancellor of the Directorate of Education.

sentences.zh: 先是，中宗遺製睿宗輔政，宗楚客、韋溫等改削槁草，嗣立時在政事府，不能正之。

translations.literal: Earlier, Emperor Zhongzong's testamentary edict had Emperor Ruizong assist in government; Zong Chuke, Wei Wen, and others revised and cut the draft — Sili was then in the chief council office and could not set it right.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Emperor Zhongzong's death edict had named Emperor Ruizong to assist in government, but Zong Chuke, Wei Wen, and others altered the draft; Sili was then in the chief council and failed to stop them.

sentences.zh: 至是為憲司所劾，左遷岳州別駕。

translations.literal: At this time he was impeached by the censorate and demoted to Assistant Administrator of Yuezhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was then impeached by the censorate and demoted to Assistant Administrator of Yuezhou.

sentences.zh: 久之，遷陳州刺史。

translations.literal: After a long while, he was transferred to Prefect of Chenzhou.
translations.idiomatic: After some time he was transferred to Prefect of Chenzhou.

sentences.zh: 時河南道巡察使、工部尚書劉知柔奏嗣立清白可陟之狀，詔命未下，開元七年卒，贈兵部尚書，諡曰孝。

translations.literal: At that time the Henan Circuit inspection commissioner and Minister of Works Liu Zhirou memorialized Sili's condition of integrity fit for promotion; the edict had not yet been issued when in the seventh year of Kaiyuan he died — posthumously granted Minister of War, posthumous title Filial.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Liu Zhirou, inspection commissioner of the Henan Circuit and Minister of Works, memorialized recommending Sili for promotion on account of his integrity; before the edict was issued, Sili died in 719. He was posthumously made Minister of War and given the posthumous title Filial.

sentences.zh: 中書門下又奏：“嗣立衣冠之內，夙表才名；

translations.literal: The Chancellery and Secretariat further memorialized, "Within the ranks of officials, Sili long displayed talent and fame;
translations.idiomatic: The Chancellery and Secretariat further memorialized: "Among officials, Sili had long been known for talent and reputation;

sentences.zh: 兄弟之間，特稱和睦。

translations.literal: Among brothers, he was especially called harmonious.
translations.idiomatic: among his brothers he was especially noted for harmony.

sentences.zh: 承恩曆事，位列宰臣。

translations.literal: Receiving grace through successive service, he ranked among chief ministers.
translations.idiomatic: Favored through successive offices, he rose to the rank of chief minister.

sentences.zh: 中年以不能正身，頗近凶戚，為憲司糾劾，因茲出貶。

translations.literal: In mid-age, because he could not rectify himself, he closely associated with villainous relatives, was impeached by the censorate, and for this reason was demoted and sent out.
translations.idiomatic: In middle age, because he failed to keep himself upright, he drew too close to disreputable kin, was impeached by the censorate, and was demoted on that account.

sentences.zh: 若循其始，終是吉人，宜棄其瑕，以從眾望。

translations.literal: If one follows from his beginning, in the end he is a good man; one should discard his flaws to follow the public's hopes.
translations.idiomatic: If one considers how he began, he was ultimately a good man; his faults should be set aside to satisfy public expectation.

sentences.zh: 請贈物一百段。”

translations.literal: We request gifting one hundred bolts of goods.
translations.idiomatic: We request that one hundred bolts of gifts be granted."

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: The request was granted.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor assented.

sentences.zh: 嗣立、承慶俱以學行齊名。

translations.literal: Silizhi and Chengqing were both equally famed for learning and conduct.
translations.idiomatic: Silizhi and Chengqing were both equally renowned for scholarship and character.

sentences.zh: 長壽中，嗣立代承慶為鳳閣舍人。

translations.literal: During the Changshou era, Silizhi replaced Chengqing as Fenige attendant.
translations.idiomatic: During the Changshou era, Silizhi succeeded Chengqing as Fenige attendant.

sentences.zh: 長安三年，承慶代嗣立為天官侍郎，頃之又代嗣立知政事。

translations.literal: In the third year of Chang'an, Chengqing replaced Silizhi as vice minister of the Ministry of Personnel; shortly after he also replaced Silizhi in managing state affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Chang'an, Chengqing took Silizhi's place as Vice Minister of Personnel; soon afterward he also replaced him in managing state affairs.

sentences.zh: 及承慶卒，嗣立又代為黃門侍郎，前後四職相代。

translations.literal: When Chengqing died, Silizhi again replaced him as vice minister of the Chancellery; in succession four posts were exchanged between them.
translations.idiomatic: When Chengqing died, Silizhi again succeeded him as Vice Minister of the Chancellery; in all, four offices passed back and forth between them.

sentences.zh: 又父子三人，皆至宰相。

translations.literal: Moreover, three generations of father and sons all reached chief minister.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, father and two sons—all three—rose to chief minister.

sentences.zh: 有唐已來，莫與為比。

translations.literal: Since the Tang dynasty began, none can compare.
translations.idiomatic: Since the founding of the Tang, none could match them.

sentences.zh: 嗣立三子：孚、恒、濟，皆知名。

translations.literal: Silizhi had three sons: Fu, Heng, and Ji — all were well known.
translations.idiomatic: Silizhi had three sons—Fu, Heng, and Ji—all of whom were well known.

sentences.zh: 孚，累遷至左司員外郎。

translations.literal: Fu rose through successive promotions to supernumerary director of the Left Department.
translations.idiomatic: Fu rose through successive promotions to Supernumerary Director of the Left Department.

sentences.zh: 恒，開元初為碭山令。

translations.literal: Heng, at the beginning of Kaiyuan, served as magistrate of Dangshan.
translations.idiomatic: Heng served as Magistrate of Dangshan at the beginning of the Kaiyuan era.

sentences.zh: 為政寬惠，人吏愛之。

translations.literal: In governance he was lenient and benevolent; officials and people loved him.
translations.idiomatic: His administration was lenient and benevolent, and officials and commoners alike loved him.

sentences.zh: 會車駕東巡，縣當供帳，時山東州縣皆懼不辦，務於鞭撲，恒獨不杖罰而事皆濟理，遠近稱焉。

translations.literal: When the imperial carriage toured eastward, the county was responsible for provisioning; at that time counties and prefectures east of the mountains all feared they could not manage it and resorted to flogging; Heng alone used no beating or punishment yet all affairs were successfully handled — near and far praised him.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor toured eastward, the county had to provide for the imperial retinue; counties and prefectures across the eastern provinces feared they could not meet the burden and relied on flogging, but Heng alone used neither staff nor punishment and still got everything done—earning praise far and near.

sentences.zh: 御史中丞宇文融，即恒之姑子也，嚐密薦恒有經濟之才，請以己之官秩回授，乃擢拜殿中侍御史。

translations.literal: Censor-in-chief Yuwen Rong was Heng's cousin by marriage; he once secretly recommended Heng as having talent for statecraft and requested to exchange his own rank and title for Heng's appointment — thus Heng was promoted to attending censor within the palace.
translations.idiomatic: Censor-in-Chief Yuwen Rong, Heng's cousin by marriage, once secretly recommended Heng as a man of statecraft and asked to surrender his own rank in exchange; Heng was then promoted to Attending Censor Within the Palace.

sentences.zh: 曆度支左司等員外、太常少卿、給事中。

translations.literal: He served successively as supernumerary in the Left Department of the Revenue Bureau and other posts, vice minister of ceremonies, and drafting attendant.
translations.idiomatic: He served successively as Supernumerary Director in the Left Department of the Revenue Bureau and other posts, Vice Minister of Ceremonies, and Drafting Attendant.

sentences.zh: 二十九年，為隴右道河西黜陟使。

translations.literal: In the twenty-ninth year, he became inspection commissioner for promotion and demotion in the Hexi region of the Longyou Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-ninth year of Kaiyuan, he was made Inspection Commissioner for Promotion and Demotion in the Hexi region of the Longyou Circuit.

sentences.zh: 恒至河西時，節度使蓋嘉運恃托中貴，公為非法，兼偽敘功勞，恒抗表請劾之，人代其懼。

translations.literal: When Heng reached Hexi, military commissioner Gai Jiayun relied on favored eunuchs and acted illegally in public affairs, also falsely claiming merit; Heng submitted a memorial requesting his impeachment — people feared on his behalf.
translations.idiomatic: When Heng reached Hexi, Military Commissioner Gai Jiayun, leaning on favored eunuchs, abused his office and falsified his record of merit; Heng submitted a memorial demanding his impeachment, and others feared for him.

sentences.zh: 因出為陳留太守，未行而卒，時人甚傷惜之。

translations.literal: He was therefore sent out as prefect of Chenliu; before departing he died — people of the time greatly mourned and regretted it.
translations.idiomatic: He was therefore posted out as Prefect of Chenliu, but died before he could take up the post; people of the time deeply mourned his loss.

sentences.zh: 濟，早以辭翰聞。

translations.literal: Ji was early known for literary composition.
translations.idiomatic: Ji was known early on for his literary gifts.

sentences.zh: 開元初，調補鄄城令。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Kaiyuan, through regular selection he was appointed magistrate of Juancheng.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Kaiyuan, through regular selection he was appointed Magistrate of Juancheng.

sentences.zh: 時有人密奏玄宗：“今歲吏部選敘太濫，縣令非材，全不簡擇。”

translations.literal: At that time someone secretly memorialized Emperor Xuanzong: "This year's Ministry of Personnel selections are too lax; county magistrates lack talent and are not screened at all."
translations.idiomatic: At that time someone secretly memorialized Emperor Xuanzong: "This year's Ministry of Personnel selections are far too lax; county magistrates are unqualified and receive no real scrutiny."

sentences.zh: 及縣令謝官日，引入殿庭，問安人策一道，試者二百餘人，獨濟策第一，或有不書紙者。

translations.literal: On the day when county magistrates took leave of office, they were brought into the palace hall; one policy question on pacifying the people was asked; among over two hundred tested, Ji alone ranked first in his essay — some did not even write on paper.
translations.idiomatic: On the day the county magistrates took leave of office, they were brought into the palace hall and given one policy question on governing the people; of more than two hundred tested, Ji alone ranked first—some did not even write a line on paper.

sentences.zh: 擢濟為醴泉令，二十餘人還舊官，四五十人放歸習讀，侍郎盧從願、李朝隱貶為刺史。

translations.literal: Ji was promoted to magistrate of Liquan; over twenty were returned to their former posts, forty or fifty were sent home to study and read; vice ministers Lu Congyuan and Li Chaoyin were demoted to prefects.
translations.idiomatic: Ji was promoted to Magistrate of Liquan; more than twenty magistrates kept their posts, forty or fifty were sent home to study, and Vice Ministers Lu Congyuan and Li Chaoyin were demoted to prefects.

sentences.zh: 濟至醴泉，以簡易為政，人用稱之。

translations.literal: When Ji reached Liquan, he governed with simplicity and ease; the people praised him.
translations.idiomatic: When Ji took office at Liquan, he governed with simplicity and ease, and the people praised him.

sentences.zh: 三遷為庫部員外郎。

translations.literal: After three promotions he became supernumerary director of the Treasury Bureau.
translations.idiomatic: After three promotions he became Supernumerary Director of the Treasury Bureau.

sentences.zh: 二十四年，為尚書戶部侍郎。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fourth year, he became vice minister of revenue in the Ministry of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-fourth year of Kaiyuan, he became Vice Minister of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 累歲轉太原尹。

translations.literal: Over successive years he was transferred to governor of Taiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Over the next several years he was transferred to Governor of Taiyuan.

sentences.zh: 製《先德詩》四章，述祖、父之行，辭致高雅。

translations.literal: He composed four chapters of "Poems of Prior Virtue," narrating his grandfather's and father's conduct — the wording refined and lofty.
translations.idiomatic: He composed four chapters of Poems of Prior Virtue recounting the conduct of his grandfather and father; the language was refined and elevated.

sentences.zh: 天寶七載，又為河南尹，遷尚書左丞。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Tianbao, he again served as governor of Henan and was transferred to left vice director of the Ministry of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year of Tianbao, he again served as Governor of Henan and was transferred to Left Vice Director of the Ministry of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 三代為省轄，衣冠榮之。

translations.literal: Three generations held central ministry posts; the gentry honored them.
translations.idiomatic: Three generations served in the central ministries—a distinction the gentry greatly admired.

sentences.zh: 濟從容雅度，所蒞人推善政，後出為馮翊太守。

translations.literal: Ji had a calm and elegant bearing; wherever he served people praised his good governance; later he was sent out as prefect of Pingyi.
translations.idiomatic: Ji had a calm and dignified bearing; wherever he served, people praised his good governance; later he was posted out as Prefect of Pingyi.

sentences.zh: 陸元方，蘇州吳縣人。

translations.literal: Lu Yuanfang, a native of Wuxian in Suzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Yuanfang was a native of Wuxian in Suzhou.

sentences.zh: 世為著姓。

translations.literal: For generations an eminent clan.
translations.idiomatic: His family had been an eminent clan for generations.

sentences.zh: 曾祖琛，陳給事中黃門侍郎。

translations.literal: Great-grandfather Chen, drafting attendant and vice minister of the Chancellery under Chen.
translations.idiomatic: His great-grandfather Chen served the Chen dynasty as Drafting Attendant and Vice Minister of the Chancellery.

sentences.zh: 伯父柬之，以工書知名，官至太子司議郎。

translations.literal: Paternal uncle Jianzhi, famous for excellence in calligraphy, reached the post of remonstrance officer of the crown prince.
translations.idiomatic: His paternal uncle Jianzhi was famous for his calligraphy and rose to Remonstrance Officer of the Crown Prince.

sentences.zh: 元方舉明經，又應八科舉，累轉監察御史。

translations.literal: Yuanfang passed the Mingjing examination and also responded to the Eight Special Examinations; through successive transfers he became supervising censor.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanfang passed the Mingjing examination and also took the Eight Special Examinations; through successive transfers he became Supervising Censor.

sentences.zh: 則天革命，使元方安輯嶺外。

translations.literal: When Empress Wu carried out her revolution, she sent Yuanfang to pacify the regions beyond the Ling mountains.
translations.idiomatic: When Empress Wu seized power, she sent Yuanfang to pacify the regions south of the Ling Mountains.

sentences.zh: 將涉海，時風濤甚壯，舟人莫敢舉帆。

translations.literal: About to cross the sea — at the time winds and waves were very fierce; the boatmen dared not raise sail.
translations.idiomatic: When he was about to cross the sea, the wind and waves ran very high, and the boatmen dared not raise sail.

sentences.zh: 元方曰：“我受命無私，神豈害我？”

translations.literal: Yuanfang said, "I received my commission without private motive — would the spirits harm me?"
translations.idiomatic: Yuanfang said, "I received my commission without private motive—would the spirits harm me?"

sentences.zh: 遽命之濟，既而風濤果息。

translations.literal: He immediately ordered them to cross; afterward the winds and waves indeed subsided.
translations.idiomatic: He immediately ordered them to set out, and the wind and waves soon subsided.

sentences.zh: 使還稱旨，除殿中侍御史。

translations.literal: Returning from his mission with approval, he was appointed attending censor within the palace.
translations.idiomatic: When he returned from his mission with the emperor's approval, he was appointed Attending Censor Within the Palace.

sentences.zh: 即以其月擢拜鳳閣舍人，仍判侍郎事。

translations.literal: That same month he was promoted to Fenige attendant, still exercising the duties of vice minister.
translations.idiomatic: That same month he was promoted to Fenige attendant and continued to discharge the duties of a vice minister.

sentences.zh: 俄為來俊臣所陷，則天手敕特赦之。

translations.literal: Soon he was framed by Lai Junchen; Empress Wu personally issued a special edict pardoning him.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was framed by Lai Junchen, but Empress Wu personally issued a special edict pardoning him.

sentences.zh: 長壽二年，再遷鸞台侍郎、同鳳閣鸞台平章事。

translations.literal: In the second year of Changshou, he was again promoted to vice minister of the Phoenix Terrace and associate director of the Fenige and Phoenix Terrace.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Changshou, he was again promoted to Vice Minister of the Phoenix Terrace and Associate Chief Minister.

sentences.zh: 延載初，又加鳳閣侍郎。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Yanzai, he was further given the title vice minister of the Fenige.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Yanzai era, he was further made Vice Minister of the Fenige.

sentences.zh: 證聖初，內史李昭德得罪，以元方附會昭德，貶綏州刺史。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Zhengsheng, inner secretary Li Zhaode fell from grace; because Yuanfang had sided with Zhaode, he was demoted to prefect of Suizhou.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Zhengsheng era, Inner Secretary Li Zhaode fell from favor; because Yuanfang had sided with him, Yuanfang was demoted to Prefect of Suizhou.

sentences.zh: 尋復為春官侍郎，又轉天官侍郎、尚書左丞，尋拜鸞台侍郎、平章事。

translations.literal: Soon he was again made vice minister of rites; then transferred to vice minister of personnel and left vice director of the Ministry of Revenue; soon appointed vice minister of the Phoenix Terrace and director of affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was restored as Vice Minister of Rites, then transferred to Vice Minister of Personnel and Left Vice Director of the Ministry of Revenue, and soon afterward appointed Vice Minister of the Phoenix Terrace and Chief Minister.

sentences.zh: 則天嚐問以外事，對曰：“臣備位宰臣，有大事即奏，人間碎務，不敢以煩聖覽。”

translations.literal: Empress Wu once asked about outside affairs; he replied, "Your servant holds a chief minister's post in name — when there are great matters I will memorialize; petty affairs of the human world I dare not trouble the sacred gaze with."
translations.idiomatic: Empress Wu once asked him about affairs outside the court; he replied, "Your servant holds a chief minister's post in name only—when there are great matters I will memorialize; petty affairs of the world I dare not trouble Your Majesty's attention with."

sentences.zh: 由是忤旨，責授太子右庶子，罷知政事。

translations.literal: For this he offended her wishes; he was punished by appointment as right supervisor of the crown prince's household and removed from managing state affairs.
translations.idiomatic: For this he gave offense; he was punished with appointment as Right Supervisor of the Crown Prince's Household and removed from managing state affairs.

sentences.zh: 尋轉文昌左丞，病卒。

translations.literal: Soon transferred to left vice director of the Literary Brilliance Department; he died of illness.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he was transferred to Left Vice Director of the Literary Brilliance Department, where he died of illness.

sentences.zh: 元方在官淸謹，再爲宰相，則天將有遷除，毎行以訪之，必密封以進，未嘗露其私恩。

translations.literal: Yuanfang was scrupulous and careful in office; twice chief minister — when Empress Wu was about to make appointments and promotions, on each journey she consulted him; he always sealed his recommendations before submitting, never once revealing private favoritism.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanfang was scrupulous and careful in office; twice chief minister—whenever Empress Wu was about to make appointments and promotions, she consulted him on her travels; he always sealed his recommendations before submitting them and never once showed private favoritism.

sentences.zh: 臨終，取前後草奏悉命焚之，且曰：“吾陰德於人多矣，其後庶幾福不衰矣。”

translations.literal: At life's end, he gathered all his draft memorials and ordered them burned, saying, "I have performed hidden virtue for many people; hereafter perhaps my fortune will not decline."
translations.idiomatic: At the end of his life he gathered all his draft memorials and ordered them burned, saying, "I have done much hidden good for others; perhaps my descendants' fortune will not fail."

sentences.zh: 又有書一匣，常自緘封，家人莫有見者，及卒視之，乃前後敕書，其慎密如此。

translations.literal: There was also a box of writings, always sealed by himself — no family member had seen it; after his death they looked and found it contained successive imperial edicts — such was his discretion.
translations.idiomatic: There was also a box of documents, always sealed by his own hand, which no member of his household had ever seen; after his death they opened it and found it contained successive imperial edicts—such was his discretion.

sentences.zh: 贈越州都督。

translations.literal: Posthumously granted defender-general of Yuezhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously made Defender-General of Yuezhou.

sentences.zh: 開元十八年，又贈揚州大都督。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year of Kaiyuan, further posthumously granted defender-general-in-chief of Yangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighteenth year of Kaiyuan, he was further posthumously made Defender-General-in-Chief of Yangzhou.

sentences.zh: 子象先。

translations.literal: (His son Xiangxian.)
translations.idiomatic: (His son Xiangxian.)

sentences.zh: 象先，本名景初。

translations.literal: Xiangxian — original name Jingchu.
translations.idiomatic: Xiangxian—his original name was Jingchu.

sentences.zh: 少有器量，應製舉，拜揚州參軍。

translations.literal: In youth he had capacity and bearing; he responded to the imperial examination and was appointed staff officer of Yangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: From youth he showed capacity and bearing; he passed an imperial examination and was appointed Staff Officer of Yangzhou.

sentences.zh: 秩滿調選，時吉頊為吏部侍郎，擢授洛陽尉，元方時亦為吏部，固辭不敢當。

translations.literal: When his term ended and he entered regular selection, at the time Ji Xu was vice minister of the Ministry of Personnel and selected him for Luoyang assistant magistrate; Yuanfang was then also in the Ministry of Personnel and firmly declined, not daring to accept.
translations.idiomatic: When his term ended and he entered regular selection, Ji Xu was Vice Minister of Personnel and selected him for Luoyang Assistant Magistrate; Yuanfang was then also serving in the Ministry of Personnel and firmly declined, not daring to accept.

sentences.zh: 頊曰：“為官擇人，至公之道。

translations.literal: Ji Xu said, "In office one selects men — this is the way of utmost fairness.
translations.idiomatic: Ji Xu said, "In office one selects the man—this is the way of utmost fairness.

sentences.zh: 陸景初才望高雅，非常流所及，實不以吏部之子妄推薦也。”

translations.literal: Lu Jingchu has talent and repute refined and lofty, beyond what the ordinary run can reach — in truth I do not recklessly recommend him because he is the Ministry of Personnel's son.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Jingchu has talent and reputation refined and lofty, beyond what ordinary men can reach—I am not recklessly recommending him simply because he is the son of a Ministry of Personnel official."

sentences.zh: 竟奏授之。

translations.literal: In the end he memorialized and granted the appointment.
translations.idiomatic: In the end he memorialized and the appointment was granted.

sentences.zh: 遷左臺監察御史，轉殿中，暦授中書侍郎。

translations.literal: Promoted to supervising censor of the Left Office; transferred to within the palace; successively appointed vice minister of the Central Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Supervising Censor of the Left Office, transferred to service within the palace, and successively appointed Vice Minister of the Central Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 景雲二年冬，同中書門下平章事，監修國史。

translations.literal: In the second year of Jingyun, winter, associate director of the Chancellery and Secretariat; supervised compilation of the national history.
translations.idiomatic: In the winter of the second year of Jingyun, he became Associate Director of the Chancellery and Secretariat and supervised compilation of the national history.

sentences.zh: 初，太平公主將引中書侍郎崔湜知政事，密以告之，湜固讓象先，主不許之，湜因亦請辭。

translations.literal: Initially, Princess Taiping was about to bring in vice minister of the Central Secretariat Cui Shi to manage state affairs and secretly told him; Cui firmly yielded to Xiangxian; the Princess did not permit it; Cui therefore also requested to decline.
translations.idiomatic: At first Princess Taiping intended to bring in Vice Minister of the Central Secretariat Cui Shi to manage state affairs and secretly told him; Cui firmly yielded the place to Xiangxian, but the Princess would not allow it, and Cui therefore asked to decline as well.

sentences.zh: 主遽言於睿宗，乃並拜焉。

translations.literal: The Princess hastily spoke to Emperor Ruizong, and both were appointed.
translations.idiomatic: The Princess hastily spoke to Emperor Ruizong, and both men were appointed.

sentences.zh: 象先清淨寡欲，不以細務介意，言論高遠，雅為時賢所服。

translations.literal: Xiangxian was pure and free of desires, unconcerned with minor affairs; his discourse lofty and far-reaching — he was properly admired by the worthy of the age.
translations.idiomatic: Xiangxian was pure and free of desire, unconcerned with petty affairs; his discourse was lofty and far-reaching, and the worthy men of the age properly admired him.

sentences.zh: 湜每謂人曰：“陸公加於人一等。”

translations.literal: Cui Shi often told people, "Lord Lu is a grade above other men."
translations.idiomatic: Cui Shi often told people, "Lord Lu is a cut above the rest."

sentences.zh: 太平公主時既用事，同時宰相蕭至忠、岑義及湜等鹹傾附之，唯象先孤立，未嚐造謁。

translations.literal: At that time Princess Taiping already held power; fellow chief ministers Xiao Zhizhong, Cen Yi, and Cui Shi all leaned toward and attached themselves to her — Xiangxian alone stood apart, never once paying a visit.
translations.idiomatic: By then Princess Taiping already held power; fellow chief ministers Xiao Zhizhong, Cen Yi, and Cui Shi all leaned toward her, but Xiangxian alone stood apart and never once paid her a visit.

sentences.zh: 先天二年，至忠等伏誅，象先獨免其難。

translations.literal: In the second year of Xiantian, Zhizhong and others were executed; Xiangxian alone escaped the calamity.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Xiantian, Zhizhong and the others were executed; Xiangxian alone escaped the calamity.

sentences.zh: 以保護功封兗國公，賜實封二百戶，加銀青光祿大夫。

translations.literal: For his protective merit he was enfeoffed as duke of Yan, granted two hundred taxable households, and given the extra title grand master of brilliant happiness with silver seal.
translations.idiomatic: For his protective service he was enfeoffed as Duke of Yan, granted two hundred taxable households, and given the title Grand Master of Brilliant Happiness with Silver Seal.

sentences.zh: 時窮討至忠等枝黨，連累稍眾，象先密有申理，全濟甚多，然未嚐言及，當時無知之者。

translations.literal: At the time the thorough pursuit of Zhizhong's branch and faction implicated many; Xiangxian secretly intervened on their behalf and saved many — yet he never spoke of it; at the time none knew.
translations.idiomatic: At the time the thorough pursuit of Zhizhong's faction implicated many people; Xiangxian secretly intervened on their behalf and saved a great number, yet he never spoke of it, and at the time no one knew.

sentences.zh: 其年，出為益州大都督府長史，仍為劍南道按察使。

translations.literal: That year he was sent out as chief administrator of the Great Protectorate General of Yizhou, still serving as inspection commissioner of the Jiannan Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: That year he was posted out as Chief Administrator of the Great Protectorate General of Yizhou and continued to serve as Inspection Commissioner of the Jiannan Circuit.

sentences.zh: 在官務以寬仁為政，司馬韋抱真言曰：“望明公稍行杖罰，以立威名。

translations.literal: In office he focused on lenient and benevolent governance; assistant administrator Wei Baozhen said, "I hope Your Excellency will somewhat apply beating and punishment to establish a reputation for authority.
translations.idiomatic: In office he focused on lenient and benevolent governance; Assistant Administrator Wei Baozhen said, "I hope Your Excellency will apply beating and punishment from time to time to establish your authority.

sentences.zh: 不然，恐下人怠墮，無所懼也。”

translations.literal: Otherwise I fear subordinates will grow idle and negligent, with nothing to fear.
translations.idiomatic: Otherwise I fear your subordinates will grow idle and negligent, with nothing to fear."

sentences.zh: 象先曰：“為政者理則可矣，何必嚴刑樹威。

translations.literal: Xiangxian said, "For one who governs, order is sufficient — why must one use harsh punishments to build authority?
translations.idiomatic: Xiangxian said, "For one who governs, order is enough—why must one use harsh punishments to build authority?

sentences.zh: 損人益己，恐非仁恕之道。”」

translations.literal: Harming others to benefit oneself — I fear this is not the way of benevolence and forbearance.
translations.idiomatic: Harming others to benefit oneself—I fear that is not the way of benevolence and forbearance."

sentences.zh: 竟不從抱眞之言。

translations.literal: In the end he did not follow Baozhen's advice.
translations.idiomatic: In the end he did not follow Baozhen's advice.

sentences.zh: 暦遷河中尹。

translations.literal: Successively transferred to governor of Hezhong.
translations.idiomatic: He was successively transferred to Governor of Hezhong.

sentences.zh: 六年，廢河中府，依舊爲蒲州，象先爲刺史，仍爲河東道按察使。

translations.literal: In the sixth year, the Hezhong Prefecture was abolished and restored as Puzhou as before; Xiangxian was prefect, still serving as inspection commissioner of the Hedong Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year, the Hezhong Prefecture was abolished and restored as Puzhou; Xiangxian became Prefect and continued to serve as Inspection Commissioner of the Hedong Circuit.

sentences.zh: 嚐有小人犯罪，但示語而遣之。

translations.literal: Once a petty offender committed a crime — he only spoke to him and sent him away.
translations.idiomatic: Once a petty offender committed a crime; Xiangxian only spoke to him and sent him away.

sentences.zh: 錄事白曰：“此例當合與杖。”

translations.literal: The recording clerk reported, "By precedent this case should receive beating."
translations.idiomatic: The recording clerk reported, "By precedent this case calls for a beating."

sentences.zh: 象先曰：“人情相去不遠，此豈不解吾言？

translations.literal: Xiangxian said, "Human feelings do not differ by much — would he not understand my words?
translations.idiomatic: Xiangxian said, "Human nature does not differ by much—would he not understand what I mean?

sentences.zh: 若必須行杖，即當自汝為始。”

translations.literal: If beating must be applied, then it should begin with you.
translations.idiomatic: If a beating must be applied, then let it begin with you."

sentences.zh: 錄事慚懼而退。

translations.literal: The recording clerk withdrew in shame and fear.
translations.idiomatic: The recording clerk withdrew in shame and fear.

sentences.zh: 象先嚐謂人曰：“天下本自無事，隻是庸人擾之，始為繁耳。

translations.literal: Xiangxian once told people, "Under Heaven there originally are no affairs — only mediocrities stir things up, and then they become complicated.
translations.idiomatic: Xiangxian once said, "Under Heaven there are originally no affairs—it is only mediocrities who stir things up and make them complicated.

sentences.zh: 但當靜之於源，則亦何憂不簡。”

translations.literal: One need only still them at the source — then why worry that things will not be simple?
translations.idiomatic: Still them at the source, and why worry that affairs will not be simple?"

sentences.zh: 前後為刺史，其政如一，人吏鹹懷思之。

translations.literal: Before and after, as prefect, his governance was the same; officials and people all cherished and remembered him.
translations.idiomatic: Before and after, as prefect, his governance was the same; officials and commoners alike cherished and remembered him.

sentences.zh: 按察使停，入為太子詹事，曆工部尚書。

translations.literal: When the inspection commissioner post was abolished, he entered the capital as grand mentor of the crown prince; successively minister of works.
translations.idiomatic: When the inspection commissioner post was abolished, he entered the capital as Grand Mentor of the Crown Prince and later served as Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 十年冬，知吏部選事，又加刑部尚書，以繼母憂免官。

translations.literal: In the tenth year, winter, he managed the Ministry of Personnel selection affairs; also given the added post of minister of justice; dismissed from office due to mourning for his stepmother.
translations.idiomatic: In the winter of the tenth year he managed Ministry of Personnel selection affairs and was also given the added post of Minister of Justice; he was dismissed from office to mourn his stepmother.

sentences.zh: 十三年，起復同州刺史，尋遷太子少保。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year, recalled from mourning as prefect of Tongzhou; soon transferred to junior mentor of the crown prince.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year he was recalled from mourning as Prefect of Tongzhou and soon transferred to Junior Mentor of the Crown Prince.

sentences.zh: 二十四年卒，年七十二，贈尚書左丞相，諡曰文貞。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fourth year he died, age seventy-two; posthumously granted left director of the Ministry of Revenue; posthumous title Wenzhen.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-fourth year he died at seventy-two; he was posthumously made Left Director of the Ministry of Revenue and given the posthumous title Wenzhen.

sentences.zh: 象先弟景倩，曆監察御史。

translations.literal: Xiangxian's younger brother Jingqian served successively as supervising censor.
translations.idiomatic: Xiangxian's younger brother Jingqian served as Supervising Censor.

sentences.zh: 景融，曆大理正、滎陽郡太守、河南尹、兵吏部侍郎、左右丞、工部尚書、東都留守、襄陽郡太守、陳留郡太守，並兼采訪使。

translations.literal: Jingrong served successively as director of the Court of Judicial Review, prefect of Xingyang Commandery, governor of Henan, vice minister of war and personnel, left and right vice directors, minister of works, eastern capital garrison commander, prefect of Xiangyang Commandery, prefect of Chenliu Commandery — all concurrently as touring commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Jingrong served successively as Director of the Court of Judicial Review, Prefect of Xingyang Commandery, Governor of Henan, Vice Minister of War and Personnel, Left and Right Vice Director, Minister of Works, Eastern Capital Garrison Commander, Prefect of Xiangyang Commandery, and Prefect of Chenliu Commandery—all concurrently as Touring Commissioner.

sentences.zh: 景獻，曆殿中侍御史、屯田員外郎。

translations.literal: Jingxian served successively as attending censor within the palace and supernumerary director of the Directorate of Public Works.
translations.idiomatic: Jingxian served successively as Attending Censor Within the Palace and Supernumerary Director of the Directorate of Public Works.

sentences.zh: 景裔，河南令、庫部郎中。

translations.literal: Jingyi — magistrate of Henan, director of the Treasury Bureau.
translations.idiomatic: Jingyi served as Magistrate of Henan and Director of the Treasury Bureau.

sentences.zh: 皆有美譽。

translations.literal: All had fine reputations.
translations.idiomatic: All enjoyed fine reputations.

sentences.zh: 僧一行少時，嚐與象先昆弟相善，常謂人曰：“陸氏兄弟皆有才行，古之荀、陳，無以加也。”

translations.literal: When the monk Yixing was young, he once was on good terms with Xiangxian and his brothers; he often told people, "The Lu brothers all have talent and conduct — the ancient Xun and Chen clans cannot surpass them."
translations.idiomatic: When the monk Yixing was young, he was on good terms with Xiangxian and his brothers; he often said, "The Lu brothers all have talent and character—the ancient clans of Xun and Chen could not surpass them."

sentences.zh: 其為當時所稱如此。

translations.literal: Thus was he praised by people of the age.
translations.idiomatic: Such was the praise he received in his day.

sentences.zh: 元方從叔餘慶，陳右軍將軍珣孫也。

translations.literal: Yuqing, collateral uncle of Yuanfang, was grandson of Xun, Right Army General of Chen.
translations.idiomatic: Yuqing, a collateral uncle of Yuanfang, was grandson of Xun, Right Army General of Chen.

sentences.zh: 少與知名之士陳子昂、宋之問、盧藏用、道士司馬承禎、道人法成等交遊，雖才學不逮子昂等，而風流強辯過之。

translations.literal: In youth he associated with renowned figures such as Chen Zi'ang, Song Zhiwen, Lu Cangyong, the Daoist priest Sima Chengzhen, the Buddhist monk Facheng, and others; though his talent and learning did not match Zi'ang and the rest, in elegance and forceful eloquence he surpassed them.
translations.idiomatic: In his youth he moved in circles with renowned men such as Chen Zi'ang, Song Zhiwen, Lu Cangyong, the Daoist priest Sima Chengzhen, the monk Facheng, and others; though his talent and learning fell short of Zi'ang and his peers, he surpassed them in charm and forceful eloquence.

sentences.zh: 累遷中書舍人。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to Secretariat draftee.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through successive promotions to Secretariat Draftee.

sentences.zh: 則天嚐引入草詔，餘慶惶惑，至晚竟不能措一辭，責授左司郎中。

translations.literal: Empress Wu once summoned him to draft an edict; Yuqing was flustered and confused, and by evening still could not put together a single phrase; he was stripped of his post and made director of the Left Office.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Wu once summoned him to draft an edict; Yuqing was flustered and, by evening, still could not compose a single line. He was demoted and appointed Director of the Left Office.

sentences.zh: 累除大理卿、散騎常侍、太子詹事。

translations.literal: He was successively removed and appointed director of the Court of Judicial Review, attendant-in-ordinary, and grand mentor of the crown prince.
translations.idiomatic: He served successively as Director of the Court of Judicial Review, Attendant-in-Ordinary, and Grand Mentor of the Crown Prince.

sentences.zh: 以老疾致仕，尋卒。

translations.literal: Due to old age and illness he retired from office; soon after he died.
translations.idiomatic: He retired due to old age and illness and died soon afterward.

sentences.zh: 象先四代孫。

translations.literal: A fourth-generation descendant of Xiangxian.
translations.idiomatic: He was a fourth-generation descendant of Xiangxian.

sentences.zh: 文宗太和四年，除釋褐參軍文學。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Taihe of Emperor Wenzong, he was appointed newly commissioned literary aide.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of the Taihe era under Emperor Wenzong, he was appointed Literary Aide upon first taking office.

sentences.zh: 蘇瓌，字昌容，京兆武功人，隋尚書右僕射威曾孫也。

translations.literal: Su Gui, courtesy name Changrong, was a native of Wugong in Jingzhao; he was great-grandson of Wei, Right Vice Director of the Ministry of Revenue of Sui.
translations.idiomatic: Su Gui, courtesy name Changrong, was a native of Wugong in Jingzhao and great-grandson of Wei, Right Vice Director of the Ministry of Revenue under the Sui.

sentences.zh: 祖夔，隋鴻臚卿。

translations.literal: His grandfather Kui was director of the Court of Diplomatic Reception under Sui.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Kui served as Director of the Court of Diplomatic Reception under the Sui.

sentences.zh: 父亶，貞觀中台州刺史。

translations.literal: His father Dan was prefect of Taizhou during the Zhenguan era.
translations.idiomatic: His father Dan served as Prefect of Taizhou in the Zhenguan period.

sentences.zh: 瓌弱冠本州舉進士，累授豫王府錄事參軍。

translations.literal: At the capping age Gui was nominated as jinshi by his home prefecture; he was repeatedly appointed recording officer of the Prince of Yu's household.
translations.idiomatic: At his capping age Gui was nominated as jinshi by his home prefecture and was repeatedly appointed Recording Officer of the Prince of Yu's household.

sentences.zh: 長史王德真、司馬劉禕之皆器重之。

translations.literal: Chief administrator Wang Dezhen and vice administrator Liu Yizhi both held him in high regard.
translations.idiomatic: Chief Administrator Wang Dezhen and Vice Administrator Liu Yizhi both esteemed him highly.

sentences.zh: 長安中，累遷揚州大都督府長史。

translations.literal: During the Chang'an era, he was repeatedly promoted to chief administrator of the Yangzhou Metropolitan Area Command.
translations.idiomatic: During the Chang'an era he was repeatedly promoted to Chief Administrator of the Yangzhou Metropolitan Area Command.

sentences.zh: 揚州地當衝要，多富商大賈，珠翠珍怪之產，前長史張潛、於辯機皆致之數萬，唯瓌挺身而去。

translations.literal: Yangzhou lay at a strategic crossroads, with many wealthy merchants and the products of pearls, jade, and rare treasures; previous chief administrators Zhang Qian and Yu Bianji each amassed tens of thousands, but Gui alone departed upright and untouched.
translations.idiomatic: Yangzhou stood at a strategic crossroads and was home to many wealthy merchants trading pearls, jade, and rare treasures; previous chief administrators Zhang Qian and Yu Bianji each amassed tens of thousands in gifts, but Gui alone left office upright and untouched.

sentences.zh: 神龍初，入為尚書右丞，以明習法律，多識台閣故事，特命刪定律、令、格、式。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Shenlong era, he entered the capital as right vice director of the Ministry of Revenue; because he was well versed in law and knew many precedents of the central administration, he was specially ordered to revise the statutes, ordinances, regulations, and forms.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Shenlong era he entered the capital as Right Vice Director of the Ministry of Revenue; because he was well versed in law and knew many central-administration precedents, he was specially ordered to revise the statutes, ordinances, regulations, and forms.

sentences.zh: 尋加銀青光祿大夫。

translations.literal: Soon he was additionally granted the title of Silver-Gleaming Grand Master of the Palace.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was additionally granted the title Silver-Gleaming Grand Master of the Palace.

sentences.zh: 是歲，再遷戶部尚書，奏計帳，所管戶時有六百一十五萬六千一百四十一。

translations.literal: That year he was again transferred to minister of revenue; when he submitted the census register, the households under his jurisdiction numbered 6,156,141.
translations.idiomatic: That year he was again transferred to Minister of Revenue; when he submitted the census register, the households under his jurisdiction numbered 6,156,141.

sentences.zh: 尋加侍中。

translations.literal: Soon he was additionally made attendant-in-ordinary.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was additionally made Attendant-in-Ordinary.

sentences.zh: 封淮陽縣子，充西京留守。

translations.literal: He was enfeoffed as Viscount of Huaiyang and appointed garrison commander of the Western Capital.
translations.idiomatic: He was enfeoffed as Viscount of Huaiyang and appointed Garrison Commander of the Western Capital.

sentences.zh: 時秘書員外監鄭普思謀為妖逆，雍、岐二州妖黨大發，瓌收普思係獄考訊之。

translations.literal: At the time the assistant director of the Secretariat, Zheng Pusi, plotted sedition through sorcery; the sorcerous factions in Yong and Qi prefectures rose up on a large scale, and Gui arrested Pusi, imprisoned him, and interrogated him.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Zheng Pusi, Assistant Director of the Secretariat, plotted sedition through sorcery; sorcerous factions in Yong and Qi prefectures rose up on a large scale, and Gui arrested Pusi, imprisoned him, and interrogated him.

sentences.zh: 普思妻第五氏以鬼道為韋庶人所寵，居止禁中，由是中宗特敕慰諭瓌，令釋普思之罪。

translations.literal: Pusi's wife, Lady Diwu, practiced ghostly arts and was favored by Empress Wei; she lived within the inner palace, and for this reason Emperor Zhongzong specially issued an edict comforting and instructing Gui, ordering him to release Pusi from guilt.
translations.idiomatic: Pusi's wife, Lady Diwu, practiced ghostly arts and was favored by Empress Wei; she lived within the inner palace, and for this reason Emperor Zhongzong specially issued an edict comforting Gui and ordering him to release Pusi.

sentences.zh: 瓌上言普思幻惑，罪當不赦。

translations.literal: Gui submitted a memorial stating that Pusi had deluded and bewitched the people and that his crime deserved no pardon.
translations.idiomatic: Gui submitted a memorial arguing that Pusi had deluded and bewitched the people and that his crime deserved no pardon.

sentences.zh: 中宗至京，又麵陳其狀。

translations.literal: When Emperor Zhongzong reached the capital, Gui again stated the facts to his face.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Zhongzong reached the capital, Gui again laid out the facts before him in person.

sentences.zh: 尚書左僕射魏元忠奏曰：“蘇瓌長者，其忠懇如此，願陛下察之。”

translations.literal: Left Vice Director of the Ministry of Revenue Wei Yuanzhong submitted: "Su Gui is a man of integrity, and his loyalty and earnestness are such as this — I hope Your Majesty will observe it."
translations.idiomatic: Left Vice Director of the Ministry of Revenue Wei Yuanzhong submitted: "Su Gui is a man of integrity, and his loyalty and earnestness are as you see — I hope Your Majesty will take note."

sentences.zh: 帝乃配流普思於儋州，其黨並誅。

translations.literal: The emperor then banished Pusi to Danzhou, and his faction was all executed.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor then banished Pusi to Danzhou, and his followers were all executed.

sentences.zh: 瓌遷吏部尚書，進封淮陽縣侯。

translations.literal: Gui was transferred to minister of personnel and advanced in enfeoffment to Marquis of Huaiyang.
translations.idiomatic: Gui was transferred to Minister of Personnel and advanced in enfeoffment to Marquis of Huaiyang.

sentences.zh: 景龍三年，轉尚書右僕射、同中書門下三品，進封許國公。

translations.literal: In the third year of Jinglong, he was transferred to right vice director of the Ministry of Revenue, made Grand Councilor of the Secretariat and Chancellery, and advanced in enfeoffment to Duke of Xu.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Jinglong he was transferred to Right Vice Director of the Ministry of Revenue, made Grand Councilor of the Secretariat and Chancellery, and advanced in enfeoffment to Duke of Xu.

sentences.zh: 是歲，將拜南郊，國子祭酒祝欽明希庶人旨，建議請皇后為亞獻，安樂公主為終獻。

translations.literal: That year, as the southern suburban sacrifice was about to be performed, the director of the Directorate of Education, Zhu Qinming, seeking to please the empress dowager, proposed that the empress serve as secondary offerer and Princess Anle as final offerer.
translations.idiomatic: That year, as the southern suburban sacrifice was about to be performed, Zhu Qinming, Director of the Directorate of Education, seeking to please the empress dowager, proposed that the empress serve as secondary offerer and Princess Anle as final offerer.

sentences.zh: 瓌深非其議，嚐於御前麵折欽明，帝雖悟，竟從欽明所奏。

translations.literal: Gui deeply disapproved of this proposal; he once rebuked Qinming to his face before the emperor; though the emperor came to understand, in the end he followed what Qinming had submitted.
translations.idiomatic: Gui deeply disapproved of the proposal and once rebuked Qinming to his face before the emperor; though the emperor came to understand, in the end he followed Qinming's recommendation.

sentences.zh: 公卿大臣初拜官者，例許獻食，名為“燒尾”。

translations.literal: When high ministers and great officials were first appointed to office, they were customarily permitted to present food — a practice called "burning the tail."
translations.idiomatic: When high ministers and great officials were first appointed to office, they were customarily permitted to present a feast — a practice called "burning the tail."

sentences.zh: 瓌拜僕射無所獻。

translations.literal: When Gui was appointed vice director, he presented nothing.
translations.idiomatic: When Gui took office as vice director, he offered no feast.

sentences.zh: 後因侍宴，將作大匠宗晉卿曰：“拜僕射竟不燒尾，豈不喜耶？”

translations.literal: Later, while attending a banquet, the master craftsman of the Directorate of Palace Buildings, Zong Jinqing, said, "Upon appointment as vice director he still did not burn the tail — is he not pleased?"
translations.idiomatic: Later, while attending a banquet, Zong Jinqing, Master Craftsman of the Directorate of Palace Buildings, said, "Upon appointment as vice director he still did not burn the tail — is he not pleased?"

sentences.zh: 帝默然。

translations.literal: The emperor was silent.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor fell silent.

sentences.zh: 瓌奏曰：“臣聞宰相者，主調陰陽，代天理物。

translations.literal: Gui submitted: "I have heard that a chief minister regulates yin and yang on behalf of Heaven and governs all things.
translations.idiomatic: Gui submitted: "I have heard that a chief minister regulates yin and yang on Heaven's behalf and governs all things.

sentences.zh: 今粒食踴貴，百姓不足，臣見宿衛兵至有三日不得食者。

translations.literal: Now grain is scarce and prices soar; the common people lack enough; I have seen palace guards who went as long as three days without food.
translations.idiomatic: Now grain is scarce and prices soar; the common people lack enough; I have seen palace guards go as long as three days without food.

sentences.zh: 臣愚不稱職，所以不敢燒尾。”

translations.literal: I am foolish and unfit for my post — that is why I did not dare burn the tail."
translations.idiomatic: I am foolish and unfit for my post — that is why I did not dare burn the tail."

sentences.zh: 是歲六月，與唐休璟並加監修國史。

translations.literal: In the sixth month of that year, he and Tang Xiujing were both additionally made supervisors of the compilation of the national history.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month of that year he and Tang Xiujing were both additionally made supervisors of the compilation of the national history.

sentences.zh: 四年，中宗崩，秘不發喪，韋庶人召諸宰相韋安石、韋巨源、蕭至忠、宗楚客、紀處訥、韋溫、李嶠、韋嗣立、唐休璟、趙彥昭及瓌等十九人入禁中會議。

translations.literal: In the fourth year, Emperor Zhongzong died; the death was kept secret and no mourning was announced; Empress Wei summoned the chief ministers Wei Anshi, Wei Juyuan, Xiao Zhizhong, Zong Chuke, Ji Chune, Wei Wen, Li Jiao, Wei Silizhi, Tang Xiujing, Zhao Yanzhao, Gui, and eighteen others — nineteen in all — into the inner palace for consultation.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year Emperor Zhongzong died; the death was kept secret and no mourning was announced; Empress Wei summoned the chief ministers Wei Anshi, Wei Juyuan, Xiao Zhizhong, Zong Chuke, Ji Chune, Wei Wen, Li Jiao, Wei Silizhi, Tang Xiujing, Zhao Yanzhao, Gui, and eighteen others — nineteen in all — into the inner palace for consultation.

sentences.zh: 初，遺製遣韋庶人輔少主知政事，授安國相王太尉參謀輔政。

translations.literal: Initially, the final edict entrusted Empress Wei to assist the young ruler in managing state affairs and appointed the Prince of Xiang, Grand Marshal of An, to advise and assist in governance.
translations.idiomatic: At first the final edict entrusted Empress Wei to assist the young ruler in managing state affairs and appointed the Prince of Xiang, Grand Marshal of An, to advise and assist in governance.

sentences.zh: 中書令宗楚客謂溫曰：“今須請皇太后臨朝，宜停相王輔政。

translations.literal: Secretariat Director Zong Chuke said to Wen: "Now we must request that the empress dowager preside over court; the Prince of Xiang's role in assisting governance should be stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Secretariat Director Zong Chuke said to Wen: "Now we must request that the empress dowager preside over court; the Prince of Xiang's role in assisting governance should be stopped.

sentences.zh: 且皇太后於相王居嫂叔不通問之地，甚難為儀注，理全不可。”

translations.literal: Moreover, between the empress dowager and the Prince of Xiang, as sister-in-law and younger brother-in-law, there is a realm where they do not exchange visits; it would be very difficult to arrange the ritual forms — in principle it is entirely impossible."
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, between the empress dowager and the Prince of Xiang, as sister-in-law and younger brother-in-law, there is a realm where they do not exchange visits; arranging the ritual forms would be very difficult — in principle it is entirely impossible."

sentences.zh: 瓌獨正色拒之，謂楚客等曰：“遺製是先帝意，安可更改！”

translations.literal: Gui alone sternly refused, saying to Chuke and the others: "The final edict expresses the late emperor's intent — how can it be altered!"
translations.idiomatic: Gui alone sternly refused, saying to Chuke and the others: "The final edict expresses the late emperor's intent — how can it be altered!"

sentences.zh: 楚客及韋溫大怒，遂削相王輔政而宣行焉。

translations.literal: Chuke and Wei Wen were greatly angered; they then struck the Prince of Xiang's role in assisting governance and promulgated the edict.
translations.idiomatic: Chuke and Wei Wen were greatly angered; they then struck the Prince of Xiang's role in assisting governance and promulgated the edict.

sentences.zh: 是月，韋氏敗，相王即帝位，下詔曰：“尚書右僕射、同中書門下三品、監修國史、許國公蘇瓌，自周旋近密，損益樞機，謀猷有成，匡讚無忌。

translations.literal: That month the Wei faction was defeated; the Prince of Xiang took the throne and issued an edict: "Right Vice Director of the Ministry of Revenue, Grand Councilor of the Secretariat and Chancellery, supervisor of the compilation of the national history, Duke of Xu, Su Gui — from intimate service at court, he has improved the pivot of state; his plans have succeeded and his loyal support has been without reserve.
translations.idiomatic: That month the Wei faction was defeated; the Prince of Xiang took the throne and issued an edict: "Right Vice Director of the Ministry of Revenue, Grand Councilor of the Secretariat and Chancellery, supervisor of the compilation of the national history, Duke of Xu, Su Gui — from intimate service at court he has improved the pivot of state; his plans have succeeded and his loyal support has been without reserve.

sentences.zh: 頃者遺恩顧托，先意昭明，奸回動搖，內外危逼，獨申讜議，實挫邪謀。

translations.literal: Recently, in the entrustment of final grace, his prior intent was clear and bright; when treacherous factions stirred and danger pressed within and without, he alone voiced upright counsel and truly thwarted wicked designs.
translations.idiomatic: Recently, in the entrustment of final grace, his prior intent was clear and bright; when treacherous factions stirred and danger pressed within and without, he alone voiced upright counsel and truly thwarted wicked designs.

sentences.zh: 況藩邸僚屬，念殷惟舊，無德不報，抑惟令典。

translations.literal: Moreover, as a former member of the prince's household staff, remembering past kindness — no virtue goes unrewarded — this is indeed the proper precedent.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, as a former member of the prince's household staff, remembering past kindness — no virtue goes unrewarded — this is indeed the proper precedent.

sentences.zh: 可尚書左僕射，餘如故。”

translations.literal: He may be left vice director of the Ministry of Revenue; the rest of his posts remain as before.
translations.idiomatic: He is appointed Left Vice Director of the Ministry of Revenue; the rest of his posts remain as before."

sentences.zh: 景雲元年，以老疾轉太子少傅。

translations.literal: In the first year of Jingyun, due to old age and illness he was transferred to junior mentor of the crown prince.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Jingyun, due to old age and illness he was transferred to Junior Mentor of the Crown Prince.

sentences.zh: 是歲十一月薨，贈司空、荊州大都督，諡曰文貞。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month of that year he died; he was posthumously granted minister of works and area commander of Jingzhou; posthumous title Wenzhen.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month of that year he died; he was posthumously granted Minister of Works and Area Commander of Jingzhou and given the posthumous title Wenzhen.

sentences.zh: 瓌臨終遺令薄葬，及祖載之日，官給儀仗外，唯有布車一乘，論者稱焉。

translations.literal: On his deathbed Gui left instructions for a simple burial; on the day the coffin was escorted to the tomb, apart from the official ceremonial guard there was only a single cloth-covered cart — commentators praised this.
translations.idiomatic: On his deathbed Gui left instructions for a simple burial; on the day the coffin was escorted to the tomb, apart from the official ceremonial guard there was only a single cloth-covered cart — commentators praised this.

sentences.zh: 開元二年，下詔曰：“疇庸賞善，百王攸先；

translations.literal: In the second year of Kaiyuan, an edict was issued: "Rewarding merit and honoring the good — all kings put this first;
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Kaiyuan, an edict was issued: "Rewarding merit and honoring the good — all kings put this first;

sentences.zh: 追還飾終，千載同德，故尚書左丞相、太子少傅、贈司空、荊州大都督、許國文貞公，瓌履正體道，外方內直，悉心奉上，卑身率禮。

translations.literal: restoring honors at the end of life, the same virtue through the ages — the late left director of the Ministry of Revenue, junior mentor of the crown prince, posthumously granted minister of works, area commander of Jingzhou, Duke of Xu with posthumous title Wenzhen, Gui — walked the upright path and embodied the Way, outwardly firm and inwardly straight, devoted himself in serving the throne, and humbled himself in observing ritual.
