translations.idiomatic: restoring honors at the end of life, the same virtue through the ages — the late Left Director of the Ministry of Revenue, Junior Mentor of the Crown Prince, posthumously granted Minister of Works, Area Commander of Jingzhou, Duke of Xu with posthumous title Wenzhen, Gui — walked the upright path and embodied the Way, outwardly firm and inwardly straight, devoted himself in serving the throne, and humbled himself in observing ritual.

sentences.zh: 協讚帷幄，三朝有鹽梅之任；

translations.literal: He assisted within the command tent; through three reigns he bore the task of salt and plums;
translations.idiomatic: He assisted within the command tent; through three reigns he bore the task of salt and plums;

sentences.zh: 燮諧台袞，九命為社稷之臣。

translations.literal: he harmonized the ministers' robes; through nine appointments he was a minister of the altars of soil and grain.
translations.idiomatic: he harmonized the ministers' robes; through nine appointments he was a minister of the altars of soil and grain.

sentences.zh: 先朝晏駕，釁起宮掖，國擅稱製之奸，人懷綴旒之懼。

translations.literal: When the previous emperor passed away, trouble arose within the palace; the state was usurped by the wicked who forged edicts; people harbored fear for the suspended imperial line.
translations.idiomatic: When the previous emperor passed away, trouble arose within the palace; the state was usurped by the wicked who forged edicts; people harbored fear for the suspended imperial line.

sentences.zh: 凶威孔熾，宗祀幾傾。

translations.literal: Ferocious power burned fiercely; the ancestral sacrifices nearly toppled.
translations.idiomatic: Ferocious power burned fiercely; the ancestral sacrifices nearly toppled.

sentences.zh: 顧命遺恩，太皇輔政，逆臣刊削，韋氏臨朝。

translations.literal: In the entrustment of final grace, the empress dowager assisted in governance; treacherous ministers excised provisions, and the Wei clan held court.
translations.idiomatic: In the entrustment of final grace, the empress dowager assisted in governance; treacherous ministers excised provisions, and the Wei clan held court.

sentences.zh: 遂能首發昌言，侃然正色，列諸視聽，暴於朝野。

translations.literal: Yet he was able to speak out first with upright words, stern in countenance, set before all eyes and ears, exposed throughout court and countryside.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he was able to speak out first with upright words, stern in countenance, set before all eyes and ears, exposed throughout court and countryside.

sentences.zh: 鬆檟已遠，風烈猶存，緬懷誠節，良深耿歎。

translations.literal: The pine and catalpa are long gone, yet his wind and force remain; recalling his loyal integrity, I am deeply moved with admiration and sighing.
translations.idiomatic: The pine and catalpa are long gone, yet his wind and force remain; recalling his loyal integrity, I am deeply moved with admiration and sighing.

sentences.zh: 可賜實封一百戶。”

translations.literal: He may be granted one hundred households of actual fief."
translations.idiomatic: Let one hundred households of actual fief be granted to him."

sentences.zh: 四年，詔與徐國公劉幽求配享睿宗廟庭。

translations.literal: In the fourth year, an edict ordered that he and Duke of Xu Liu Youqiu be granted paired sacrifice in the temple hall of Emperor Ruizong.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year, an edict ordered that he and Duke of Xu Liu Youqiu be granted paired sacrifice in the temple hall of Emperor Ruizong.

sentences.zh: 十七年，加贈司徒。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year, he was additionally posthumously granted minister of works.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventeenth year he was additionally posthumously granted Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 瓌子頲，少有俊才，一覽千言。

translations.literal: Gui's son Ting had outstanding talent in youth; with one reading he mastered a thousand words.
translations.idiomatic: Gui's son Ting had outstanding talent in youth; with one reading he mastered a thousand words.

sentences.zh: 弱冠舉進士，授烏程尉，累遷左台監察御史。

translations.literal: At the capping age he passed the jinshi examination; he was appointed magistrate of Wucheng and was repeatedly promoted to supervising censor of the Left Censorate.
translations.idiomatic: At his capping age he passed the jinshi examination; he was appointed Magistrate of Wucheng and was repeatedly promoted to Supervising Censor of the Left Censorate.

sentences.zh: 長安中，詔頲按覆來俊臣等舊獄，頲皆申明其枉，由此雪冤者甚眾。

translations.literal: During the Chang'an era, an edict ordered Ting to review the old cases of Lai Junchen and others; Ting clarified the injustice in each, and by this means many were cleared of wrongful charges.
translations.idiomatic: During the Chang'an era an edict ordered Ting to review the old cases of Lai Junchen and others; Ting clarified the injustice in each, and by this means many were cleared of wrongful charges.

sentences.zh: 神龍中，累遷給事中，加修文館學士，俄拜中書舍人。

translations.literal: During the Shenlong era, he was repeatedly promoted to palace attendant, additionally made a scholar of the Xiuxian Hall, and soon appointed Secretariat draftee.
translations.idiomatic: During the Shenlong era he was repeatedly promoted to Palace Attendant, additionally made a Scholar of the Xiuxian Hall, and soon appointed Secretariat Draftee.

sentences.zh: 尋而頲父同中書門下三品，父子同掌樞密，時以為榮。

translations.literal: Soon afterward Ting's father became grand councilor of the Secretariat and Chancellery; father and son together managed the pivot of state — at the time this was considered an honor.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward Ting's father became Grand Councilor of the Secretariat and Chancellery; father and son together managed the pivot of state — at the time this was considered an honor.

sentences.zh: 機事填委，文誥皆出頲手。

translations.literal: State affairs piled up in profusion; all edicts and proclamations came from Ting's hand.
translations.idiomatic: State affairs piled up in profusion; all edicts and proclamations came from Ting's hand.

sentences.zh: 中書令李嶠歎曰：“舍人思如湧泉，嶠所不及也。”

translations.literal: Secretariat Director Li Jiao sighed and said: "The draftee's thought flows like a spring — Jiao cannot match it."
translations.idiomatic: Secretariat Director Li Jiao sighed and said: "The draftee's thought flows like a spring — Jiao cannot match it."

sentences.zh: 俄遷太常少卿。

translations.literal: Soon he was transferred to vice director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was transferred to Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 景雲中，瓌薨，詔頲起復為工部侍郎，加銀青光祿大夫。

translations.literal: During the Jingyun era Gui died; an edict ordered Ting recalled from mourning as vice minister of works and additionally granted the title of Silver-Gleaming Grand Master of the Palace.
translations.idiomatic: During the Jingyun era Gui died; an edict ordered Ting recalled from mourning as Vice Minister of Works and additionally granted the title Silver-Gleaming Grand Master of the Palace.

sentences.zh: 頲抗表固辭，辭理懇切，詔許其終製。

translations.literal: Ting submitted a memorial firmly refusing; his reasoning was earnest and sincere; an edict permitted him to complete mourning.
translations.idiomatic: Ting submitted a memorial firmly refusing; his reasoning was earnest and sincere; an edict permitted him to complete mourning.

sentences.zh: 服闋就職，襲父爵許國公。

translations.literal: When mourning ended he took up his post and inherited his father's title as Duke of Xu.
translations.idiomatic: When mourning ended he took up his post and inherited his father's title as Duke of Xu.

sentences.zh: 玄宗謂宰臣曰：“有從工部侍郎得中書侍郎否？”

translations.literal: Emperor Xuanzong said to the chief ministers: "Has anyone ever gone from vice minister of works to vice director of the Secretariat?"
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xuanzong said to the chief ministers: "Has anyone ever gone from Vice Minister of Works to Vice Director of the Secretariat?"

sentences.zh: 對曰：“任賢用能，非臣等所及。”

translations.literal: They replied: "Selecting the worthy and employing the capable — that is not within our reach."
translations.idiomatic: They replied: "Selecting the worthy and employing the capable — that is not within our reach."

sentences.zh: 玄宗曰：“蘇頲可中書侍郎，仍供政事食。”

translations.literal: Emperor Xuanzong said: "Su Ting may be vice director of the Secretariat, and he shall still receive administrative provisions."
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xuanzong said: "Su Ting may be Vice Director of the Secretariat, and he shall still receive administrative provisions."

sentences.zh: 明日，加知制誥。

translations.literal: The next day he was additionally made drafter of edicts.
translations.idiomatic: The next day he was additionally made Drafter of Edicts.

sentences.zh: 有政事食，自頲始也。

translations.literal: Administrative provisions — this began with Ting.
translations.idiomatic: The practice of administrative provisions began with Ting.

sentences.zh: 頲入謝，玄宗曰：“常欲用卿，每有好官闕，即望宰相論及。

translations.literal: When Ting entered to give thanks, Emperor Xuanzong said: "I have long wished to employ you; whenever a good post fell vacant, I hoped the chief ministers would mention you.
translations.idiomatic: When Ting entered to give thanks, Emperor Xuanzong said: "I have long wished to employ you; whenever a good post fell vacant, I hoped the chief ministers would mention you.

sentences.zh: 宰相皆卿之故人，卒無言者，朕為卿歎息。

translations.literal: The chief ministers are all your old acquaintances, yet in the end none spoke — I sigh on your behalf.
translations.idiomatic: The chief ministers are all your old acquaintances, yet in the end none spoke — I sigh on your behalf.

sentences.zh: 中書侍郎，朕極重惜，自陸象先歿後，朕每思之，無出卿者。”

translations.literal: Vice director of the Secretariat — I value it extremely; since Lu Xiangxian died, I have thought of it often, and no one surpasses you."
translations.idiomatic: Vice Director of the Secretariat — I value it extremely; since Lu Xiangxian died, I have thought of it often, and no one surpasses you."

sentences.zh: 時李乂為紫微侍郎，與頲對掌文誥。

translations.literal: At the time Li Yi was vice director of the Palace Secretariat; he and Ting jointly managed edicts and proclamations.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Li Yi was Vice Director of the Palace Secretariat; he and Ting jointly managed edicts and proclamations.

sentences.zh: 他日，上謂頲曰：“前朝有李嶠、蘇味道，謂之蘇、李；

translations.literal: On another day the emperor said to Ting: "In the previous reign there were Li Jiao and Su Weidao — they were called Su and Li;
translations.idiomatic: On another day the emperor said to Ting: "In the previous reign there were Li Jiao and Su Weidao — they were called Su and Li;

sentences.zh: 今有卿及李乂，亦不讓之。

translations.literal: now with you and Li Yi, they are not inferior.
translations.idiomatic: now with you and Li Yi, they are not inferior.

sentences.zh: 卿所製文誥，可錄一本封進，題雲‘臣某撰’，朕要留中披覽。”

translations.literal: The edicts and proclamations you compose — copy one set, seal it, and submit it, titled "Composed by your subject so-and-so"; I wish to keep it within the palace and read it."
translations.idiomatic: The edicts and proclamations you compose — copy one set, seal it, and submit it, titled "Composed by your subject so-and-so"; I wish to keep it within the palace and read it."

sentences.zh: 其禮遇如此。

translations.literal: Such was the courtesy shown him.
translations.idiomatic: Such was the courtesy shown him.

sentences.zh: 玄宗欲於靖陵建碑，頲諫曰：“帝王及後，無神道碑，且事不師古，動皆不法。

translations.literal: Emperor Xuanzong wished to erect a stele at Jing Mausoleum; Ting remonstrated: "For emperors and empresses there are no spirit-way steles, and moreover the matter does not follow antiquity — every move is unlawful.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xuanzong wished to erect a stele at Jing Mausoleum; Ting remonstrated: "For emperors and empresses there are no spirit-way steles, and moreover the matter does not follow antiquity — every move is unlawful.

sentences.zh: 若靖陵獨建，陛下祖宗之陵皆須追造。”

translations.literal: If Jing Mausoleum alone has one built, the mausoleums of Your Majesty's ancestors would all have to be retroactively provided with them."
translations.idiomatic: If Jing Mausoleum alone has one built, the mausoleums of Your Majesty's ancestors would all have to be retroactively provided with them."

sentences.zh: 玄宗從其言而止。

translations.literal: Emperor Xuanzong followed his words and stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xuanzong followed his words and stopped.

sentences.zh: 開元四年，遷紫微侍郎、同紫微黃門平章事，與侍中宋璟同知政事。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Kaiyuan, he was transferred to vice director of the Palace Secretariat, made Grand Councilor of the Palace Secretariat and Chancellery, and together with Attendant-in-Ordinary Song Jing managed state affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Kaiyuan he was transferred to Vice Director of the Palace Secretariat, made Grand Councilor of the Palace Secretariat and Chancellery, and together with Attendant-in-Ordinary Song Jing managed state affairs.

sentences.zh: 璟剛正，多所裁斷，頲皆順從其美；

translations.literal: Jing was upright and firm and made many decisions; Ting always followed what was good in them;
translations.idiomatic: Jing was upright and firm and made many decisions; Ting always followed what was good in them;

sentences.zh: 若上前承旨、敷奏及應對，則頲為之助，相得甚悅。

translations.literal: when before the throne receiving the emperor's intent, presenting memorials, or responding, then Ting assisted, and the two worked together with great satisfaction.
translations.idiomatic: when before the throne receiving the emperor's intent, presenting memorials, or responding, then Ting assisted, and the two worked together with great satisfaction.

sentences.zh: 璟嚐謂人曰：“吾與蘇家父子，前後同時為宰相。

translations.literal: Jing once told people: "The Su father and son and I have successively served as chief ministers at the same time.
translations.idiomatic: Jing once told people: "The Su father and son and I have successively served as chief ministers at the same time.

sentences.zh: 僕射長厚，誠為國器；

translations.literal: The vice director was long in virtue and truly a vessel of state;
translations.idiomatic: The vice director was long in virtue and truly a vessel of state;

sentences.zh: 若獻可替否，罄盡臣節，斷割吏事，至公無私，即頲過其父也”。

translations.literal: but in offering what is acceptable and replacing what is not, exhausting ministerial duty, cutting through official business, utterly public and without private interest — in that Ting surpasses his father."
translations.idiomatic: but in offering what is acceptable and replacing what is not, exhausting ministerial duty, cutting through official business, utterly public and without private interest — in that Ting surpasses his father."

sentences.zh: 八年，除禮部尚書，罷政事。

translations.literal: In the eighth year he was appointed minister of rites and removed from managing state affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year he was appointed Minister of Rites and removed from managing state affairs.

sentences.zh: 俄知益州大都督府長史事。

translations.literal: Soon he was made acting chief administrator of the Yizhou Metropolitan Area Command.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was made acting Chief Administrator of the Yizhou Metropolitan Area Command.

sentences.zh: 前司馬皇甫恂破庫物織新樣錦以進，頲一切罷之。

translations.literal: The former military aide Huangfu Xun broke into treasury stores, wove new-pattern brocade, and presented it; Ting abolished all of it.
translations.idiomatic: The former military aide Huangfu Xun broke into the treasury stores, wove brocade in a new pattern, and presented it as tribute; Ting abolished the practice entirely.

sentences.zh: 或謂頲曰：“公今在遠，豈得忤聖意？”

translations.literal: Some said to Ting: "You are far away now — how can you go against the emperor's wish?"
translations.idiomatic: Some said to Ting: "You are far from court now — how can you defy the emperor's wish?"

sentences.zh: 頲曰：“明主不以私愛奪至公，豈以遠近間易忠臣節也！”

translations.literal: Ting said: "An enlightened ruler does not let private affection override supreme public duty — how could distance or nearness alter a loyal minister's constancy!"
translations.idiomatic: Ting said: "An enlightened ruler does not let private affection override supreme public duty — how could distance or nearness change a loyal minister's constancy!"

sentences.zh: 竟奏罷之。

translations.literal: In the end he memorialized and had it abolished.
translations.idiomatic: In the end he submitted a memorial and had it abolished.

sentences.zh: 巂州蠻酋苴院私與吐蕃連謀，將為內寇，頲獲其間諜，將士鹹請出兵討之，頲不從，乃作書並間諜以送苴院，苴院慚悔，竟不敢入寇。

translations.literal: The tribal chieftain Juyuan of Xizhou secretly plotted with Tibet and was about to raid within the borders; Ting captured his spy; officers and soldiers all asked to send troops to punish him, but Ting did not agree — instead he wrote a letter and sent it with the spy to Juyuan; Juyuan felt shame and remorse and in the end did not dare invade.
translations.idiomatic: The tribal chieftain Juyuan of Xizhou secretly plotted with Tibet and was about to raid the interior; Ting captured his spy. Officers and soldiers all urged him to send troops against the chieftain, but Ting refused. Instead he wrote a letter and sent it along with the spy to Juyuan. Ashamed and remorseful, Juyuan in the end did not dare invade.

sentences.zh: 十三年，從駕東封，玄宗令頲撰朝覲碑文。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year he accompanied the emperor on the eastern tour and fengshan rite; Emperor Xuanzong ordered Ting to compose the inscription for the imperial audience.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year he accompanied the emperor on the eastern tour and fengshan rite; Emperor Xuanzong ordered Ting to compose the inscription for the imperial audience.

sentences.zh: 俄又知吏部選事。

translations.literal: Soon he was additionally placed in charge of Ministry of Personnel selections.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was additionally placed in charge of Ministry of Personnel selections.

sentences.zh: 頲性廉儉，所得俸祿，盡推與諸弟，或散之親族，家無餘資。

translations.literal: Ting's nature was honest and frugal; the salary he received he entirely passed on to his younger brothers, or distributed among kinsmen — the household had no surplus wealth.
translations.idiomatic: Ting was honest and frugal by nature; he gave all his salary to his younger brothers or distributed it among his kin, and his household kept no surplus wealth.

sentences.zh: 十五年卒，年五十八。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year he died, age fifty-eight.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifteenth year he died, at the age of fifty-eight.

sentences.zh: 初，優贈之製未出，起居舍人韋述上疏曰：“臣伏見貞觀、永徽之時，每有公卿大臣薨卒，皆輟朝舉哀，所以成終始之恩，厚君臣之義。

translations.literal: At first, before the decree of posthumous honors had been issued, diarist-attendant Wei Shu submitted a memorial saying: "Your servant has observed that in the Zhenguan and Yonghui eras, whenever a high minister died, the court always suspended sessions and held mourning — thereby completing the grace of beginning to end and deepening the righteousness between ruler and minister.
translations.idiomatic: At first, before the decree of posthumous honors had been issued, Diarist-Attendant Wei Shu submitted a memorial saying: "Your servant has observed that in the Zhenguan and Yonghui eras, whenever a high minister died, the court always suspended sessions and held mourning—thereby completing the grace owed from first to last and deepening the bond between ruler and minister.

sentences.zh: 上有旌賢錄舊之德，下有生榮死哀之美，列於史冊，以示將來。

translations.literal: Above, there is the virtue of honoring the worthy and recording old service; below, there is the beauty of honor in life and mourning in death — recorded in the historical annals to show those who come after.
translations.idiomatic: Above, the court honors the worthy and records past service; below, men receive honor in life and mourning in death—set down in the historical annals as an example for generations to come.

sentences.zh: 昔智悼子卒，平公宴樂，杜蒯一言，言始感悟。

translations.literal: In antiquity, when Zhi Daozi died, Duke Ping feasted and made music; one word from Du Kui — only then did he awaken to the right course.
translations.idiomatic: In antiquity, when Zhi Daozi died, Duke Ping continued to feast and make music; a single remonstrance from Du Kui at last moved him to see his error.

sentences.zh: 《春秋》載其盛烈，禮經以為美談，今古舊事，昭然可睹。

translations.literal: The Spring and Autumn Annals records that splendid virtue; the ritual classics treat it as a fine tale — old affairs of past and present, clearly visible.
translations.idiomatic: The Spring and Autumn Annals records that splendid deed; the ritual classics treat it as a celebrated example—an old story from past and present, plain for all to see.

sentences.zh: 臣伏見故禮部尚書蘇頲，累葉輔弼，代傳忠清。

translations.literal: Your servant has observed the late Minister of Rites Su Ting — for generations his family served as chief ministers, transmitting loyalty and integrity through the ages.
translations.idiomatic: Your servant has observed the late Minister of Rites Su Ting—a family that for generations served as chief ministers and handed down loyalty and integrity from age to age.

sentences.zh: 頲又伏事軒陛二十餘載，入參謀猷，出總藩牧。

translations.literal: Ting moreover served humbly at the imperial throne for more than twenty years — entering to share in counsel, going out to oversee provincial administration.
translations.idiomatic: Ting moreover served humbly at the imperial throne for more than twenty years—entering court to share in counsel, going out to govern the provinces.

sentences.zh: 誠績斯著，操履無虧，天不憖遺，奄違聖代。

translations.literal: His achievements were truly manifest, his conduct without blemish — Heaven did not long preserve him, and suddenly he departed this sage age.
translations.idiomatic: His achievements were truly manifest and his conduct without blemish, yet Heaven did not long preserve him, and suddenly he departed this enlightened age.

sentences.zh: 伏願陛下思帷蓋之舊，念股肱之親，修先朝之盛典，鑒晉平之遠跡，為之輟朝舉哀，以明同體之義。

translations.literal: Your servant humbly wishes Your Majesty would recall the old bond of carriage and canopy, remember the closeness of arm and thigh, restore the grand rites of former courts, take as mirror Duke Ping of Jin's distant example, and for him suspend court and hold mourning — thereby making clear the principle that ruler and minister are one body.
translations.idiomatic: Your servant humbly wishes that Your Majesty will recall your long bond with him, remember how close he stood as your right hand, restore the grand rites of former courts, take Duke Ping of Jin's distant example to heart, and for him suspend court and hold mourning—thereby making clear that ruler and minister are one body.

sentences.zh: 使歿者荷德於泉壤，存者盡節於周行，凡百卿士，孰不幸甚。

translations.literal: Let the dead receive grace in the underworld; let the living fulfill their duty among their fellows — among all the ministers and officials, who would not be deeply fortunate?
translations.idiomatic: Let the dead receive your grace in the underworld; let the living devote themselves fully among their colleagues—among all ministers and officials, who would not count himself deeply fortunate?

sentences.zh: 臣官忝記事，君舉必書，敢申舊典，上黷宸扆，希降恩貸，俯垂詳擇。”

translations.literal: Your servant's office humbly records events — the ruler's acts must be written; I dare appeal to the old precedent, offending the imperial screen above; I hope for gracious pardon and humbly beg careful consideration."
translations.idiomatic: Your servant's office is charged with recording events—the ruler's acts must be written down—so I dare appeal to this old precedent, though it offends the imperial presence; I beg your gracious pardon and humbly ask for your careful consideration."

sentences.zh: 即日於洛城南門舉哀，輟朝兩日，贈尚書右丞相，諡曰文憲。

translations.literal: That same day mourning was held at the south gate of Luoyang; court was suspended for two days; he was posthumously granted right director of the Department of State Affairs; posthumous title Wenxian.
translations.idiomatic: That same day mourning was held at the south gate of Luoyang; court was suspended for two days; he was posthumously made Right Director of the Department of State Affairs and given the posthumous title Wenxian.

sentences.zh: 及葬日，玄宗遊咸宜宮，將出獵，聞頲喪出，愴然曰：“蘇頲今日葬，吾寧忍娛遊。”

translations.literal: On the day of the burial, Emperor Xuanzong was visiting Xianyi Palace and was about to go hunting; hearing that Ting's funeral procession had set out, he said mournfully: "Su Ting is being buried today — how could I bear to amuse myself with sport?"
translations.idiomatic: On the day of the burial, Emperor Xuanzong was at Xianyi Palace and about to go hunting; when he heard that Ting's funeral procession had set out, he said mournfully: "Su Ting is being buried today—how could I bear to amuse myself with sport?"

sentences.zh: 中路還宮。

translations.literal: Halfway there he turned back to the palace.
translations.idiomatic: Halfway there he turned back to the palace.

sentences.zh: 頲弟詵、冰、乂。

translations.literal: Ting's younger brothers were Shen, Bing, and Yi.
translations.idiomatic: Ting's younger brothers were Shen, Bing, and Yi.

sentences.zh: 詵，曆授右司郎中、給事中、徐州刺史。

translations.literal: Shen successively received appointment as director in the right bureau, attendant censor, and prefect of Xuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Shen was successively appointed Director in the Right Bureau, Attendant Censor, and Prefect of Xuzhou.

sentences.zh: 先是，拜給事中時，頲為中書侍郎，上表讓詵所授。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Shen was appointed attendant censor, Ting was vice director of the Secretariat and submitted a memorial declining the appointment given to Shen.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when Shen was appointed Attendant Censor, Ting was Vice Director of the Secretariat and submitted a memorial declining the appointment given to Shen.

sentences.zh: 玄宗曰：“古來有內舉不避親乎？”

translations.literal: Emperor Xuanzong said: "Since antiquity, has there not been recommending from within without avoiding kin?"
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xuanzong said: "Since antiquity, has there not been recommending one's own kin without favoritism?"

sentences.zh: 頲曰：“晉祁奚是也。”

translations.literal: Ting said: "Qi Xi of Jin was such a man."
translations.idiomatic: Ting said: "Qi Xi of Jin was such a man."

sentences.zh: 玄宗曰：“若然，則朕用蘇詵，何得屢言？

translations.literal: Emperor Xuanzong said: "If so, then when I employ Su Shen, why do you speak of it repeatedly?
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xuanzong said: "If so, then when I employ Su Shen, why do you speak of it again and again?

sentences.zh: 近日卿父子猶同在中書，兄弟有何不得？

translations.literal: Recently you and your father were still together in the Secretariat — why should brothers not be allowed?
translations.idiomatic: Recently you and your father were still together in the Secretariat—why should brothers not be allowed?

sentences.zh: 卿言非至公也。”

translations.literal: Your words are not utterly public-minded."
translations.idiomatic: Your words are not utterly public-minded."

sentences.zh: 冰，為虞部郎中。

translations.literal: Bing served as director in the Bureau of Parks and Forests.
translations.idiomatic: Bing served as Director in the Bureau of Parks and Forests.

sentences.zh: 乂，為職方郎中。

translations.literal: Yi served as director in the Bureau of Military Appointments.
translations.idiomatic: Yi served as Director in the Bureau of Military Appointments.

sentences.zh: 幹，瓌從父兄也。

translations.literal: Gan was Gui's father's elder brother's son.
translations.idiomatic: Gan was Gui's cousin—the son of his father's elder brother.

sentences.zh: 父勖，武德中為秦王府文學館學士。

translations.literal: His father Xu, during the Wude era, served as literary academy scholar in the Prince of Qin's household.
translations.idiomatic: His father Xu served during the Wude era as a literary academy scholar in the Prince of Qin's household.

sentences.zh: 貞觀中，尚南康公主，拜駙馬都尉，累選魏王泰府司馬。

translations.literal: During the Zhenguan era he married Princess Nankang, was appointed commandant-escort, and through successive selections became secretary in the household of Prince Tai of Wei.
translations.idiomatic: During the Zhenguan era he married Princess Nankang, was appointed Commandant-Escort, and through successive appointments became Secretary in the household of Prince Tai of Wei.

sentences.zh: 勖既博學有美名，甚為泰所重。

translations.literal: Xu was broadly learned and had a fine reputation; Tai greatly valued him.
translations.idiomatic: Xu was broadly learned and enjoyed a fine reputation; Tai greatly valued him.

sentences.zh: 因勸泰請開文學館，引才名之士，撰《括地志》。

translations.literal: Accordingly he urged Tai to request opening a literary academy, invite men of talent and renown, and compile the Comprehensive Gazetteer of the Realm.
translations.idiomatic: Accordingly he urged Tai to request the opening of a literary academy, invite men of talent and renown, and compile the Comprehensive Gazetteer of the Realm.

sentences.zh: 後曆吏部郎、太子左庶子，卒。

translations.literal: Later he successively served as director in the Ministry of Personnel and left mentor of the crown prince, then died.
translations.idiomatic: Later he served successively as Director in the Ministry of Personnel and Left Mentor of the Crown Prince, then died.

sentences.zh: 幹少以明經累授徐王府記室參軍。

translations.literal: Gan in youth, through passing the Mingjing examination, was repeatedly appointed recorder-attendant in the household of the Prince of Xu.
translations.idiomatic: In youth Gan passed the Mingjing examination and was repeatedly appointed Recorder-Attendant in the household of the Prince of Xu.

sentences.zh: 徐王好畋獵，幹每諫止之。

translations.literal: The Prince of Xu loved hunting; Gan repeatedly remonstrated and stopped him.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Xu loved hunting; Gan repeatedly remonstrated and tried to stop him.

sentences.zh: 垂拱中，曆遷魏州刺史。

translations.literal: During the Chuigong era he was successively transferred to prefect of Weizhou.
translations.idiomatic: During the Chuigong era he was successively transferred to Prefect of Weizhou.

sentences.zh: 時河北饑饉，舊吏苛酷，百姓多有逃散。

translations.literal: At the time Hebei suffered famine; the old officials were harsh and cruel, and many common people fled and scattered.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Hebei was suffering famine; the old officials were harsh and cruel, and many common people fled and scattered.

sentences.zh: 幹乃督察奸吏，務勸農桑，由是逃散者皆來復業，稱為良牧。

translations.literal: Gan then inspected and punished corrupt officials and devoted himself to encouraging agriculture and sericulture; thereby those who had fled all returned to their occupations, and he was called a good governor.
translations.idiomatic: Gan then inspected and punished corrupt officials and devoted himself to encouraging agriculture and sericulture; those who had fled all returned to their occupations, and he was acclaimed as a good governor.

sentences.zh: 召拜右羽林將軍，尋遷冬官尚書。

translations.literal: He was summoned and appointed right general of the Feathered Forest Guard; soon he was transferred to minister of works.
translations.idiomatic: He was summoned and appointed Right General of the Feathered Forest Guard; soon he was transferred to Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 酷吏來俊臣素忌嫉之，遂誣奏幹在魏州與琅邪王衝私書往復，因係獄鞫訊，幹發憤而卒。

translations.literal: The cruel official Lai Junchen had long envied and hated him; he then falsely memorialized that Gan in Weizhou exchanged private letters with Prince Langye Chong; Gan was therefore imprisoned and interrogated, and died in a fit of rage.
translations.idiomatic: The cruel official Lai Junchen had long envied and hated him; he then falsely memorialized that Gan in Weizhou had exchanged private letters with Prince Langye Chong. Gan was imprisoned and interrogated, and died in a fit of rage.

sentences.zh: 瓌四代孫翔，文宗太和四年，釋褐文學參軍。

translations.literal: Gui's fourth-generation descendant Xiang, in the fourth year of Taihe of Emperor Wenzong, took his first office as literary aide.
translations.idiomatic: Gui's fourth-generation descendant Xiang, in the fourth year of the Taihe era under Emperor Wenzong, took his first office as Literary Aide.

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：韋思謙始以州縣，奮於煙霄，持綱不避於權豪，報國能忘於妻子。

translations.literal: The historiographer says: Wei Siqian began from county and prefecture posts and rose into the clouds; he upheld the law without avoiding the powerful, and in serving the state could forget wife and children.
translations.idiomatic: The historiographer says: Wei Siqian began from county and prefecture posts and rose to the heights of power; he upheld the law without flinching before the mighty, and in serving the state could forget wife and children.

sentences.zh: 自強不息，剛毅近仁，信有之矣！

translations.literal: Ceaseless self-strengthening, resolute firmness close to benevolence — truly it was so!
translations.idiomatic: Ceaseless self-strengthening, resolute firmness close to benevolence—truly it was so!

sentences.zh: 高季輔、皇甫公義，可謂知人矣！

translations.literal: Gao Jifu and Huangfu Gongyi — one may say they knew men!
translations.idiomatic: Gao Jifu and Huangfu Gongyi—one may say they truly knew men!

sentences.zh: 且福善餘慶，不謂無徵，二子構堂，俱列相輔，文皆經濟，政盡明能。

translations.literal: Moreover, fortune follows virtue and surplus blessings remain — not to say without signs; the two sons built the hall, both ranked as chief ministers; their writings all served statecraft, their governance all clear and capable.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, fortune follows virtue and blessings accumulate for posterity—not without signs; the two sons raised the family to eminence, both rose to chief minister; their writings all served statecraft, and their governance was throughout clear and capable.

sentences.zh: 加以承慶方危，染翰而曾非恐悚；

translations.literal: Add to this that when Chengqing was in peril, he wielded the brush and was never once fearful;
translations.idiomatic: Add to this that when Chengqing was in peril, he took up the brush and showed not the slightest fear;

sentences.zh: 嗣立見用，襲封而罔墜逍遙。

translations.literal: Silizhi was employed and inherited the enfeoffment without falling from ease.
translations.idiomatic: Silizhi was employed and inherited the enfeoffment without losing his ease and dignity.

sentences.zh: 無忝父風，寧慚祖德，諡溫諡孝，何愧易名？

translations.literal: Not failing their father's style — how could they shame their ancestors' virtue? Posthumous titles Wen and Xiao — what shame in renaming?
translations.idiomatic: They did not fail their father's example—how could they shame their ancestors' virtue? Posthumous titles Wen and Xiao—what shame could there be in such names?

sentences.zh: 陸元方博學大度，再踐鈞衡，當則天時，非有忠貞，應無黜責，綏州之任，抑又何慚！

translations.literal: Lu Yuanfang was broadly learned and magnanimous, twice stepping to the chief minister's scales; in Empress Wu's time, without loyalty and steadfastness he would surely have suffered dismissal and blame — the appointment to Suizhou, what shame in that!
translations.idiomatic: Lu Yuanfang was broadly learned and magnanimous, twice serving as chief minister; in Empress Wu's time, without loyalty and steadfastness he would surely have suffered dismissal and blame—the appointment to Suizhou, what shame could there be in that!

sentences.zh: 觀其濟海無私，狂風自止，臨終焚槁，溫樹始彰。

translations.literal: Observe him crossing the sea without selfish motive — wild winds stopped of themselves; at life's end burning dry drafts — the warm tree at last became manifest.
translations.idiomatic: Observe him crossing the sea without selfish motive—the wild winds stopped of themselves; at life's end burning his draft memorials—the warm tree at last became manifest.

sentences.zh: 故知正可以動神明，德可以延家代。

translations.literal: Thus one knows rectitude can move the spirits, and virtue can extend a family through generations.
translations.idiomatic: Thus one knows that rectitude can move the spirits, and virtue can extend a family through generations.

sentences.zh: 象先益高人品，尤著相才，全濟有名，孤立無禍。

translations.literal: Xiangxian was even more elevated in personal character and especially renowned for ministerial talent; Quan Ji had a name for saving many, and standing alone he suffered no calamity.
translations.idiomatic: Xiangxian stood even higher in personal character and was especially renowned for ministerial talent; Quan Ji was famed for saving many lives, and though he stood alone he suffered no calamity.

sentences.zh: 景倩、景融、景獻、景裔等鹹居清列，得非有後於魯乎？

translations.literal: Jingqian, Jingrong, Jingxian, Jingyi, and the rest all held pure ranks — is this not having worthy successors like Lu?
translations.idiomatic: Jingqian, Jingrong, Jingxian, Jingyi, and the rest all held high office—is this not having worthy successors, as Confucius said of Lu?

sentences.zh: 蘇瓌，孔子云：“居其室，出其言善，則千里之外應之，況其邇者乎！”

translations.literal: Su Gui — Confucius said: "When one dwells in his room and his words are good, then from a thousand li away men respond — how much more those near at hand!"
translations.idiomatic: Su Gui—Confucius said: "When one dwells in his room and his words are good, then from a thousand li away men respond—how much more those near at hand!"

sentences.zh: 又“言行君子之樞機，樞機之發，榮辱之主也”。

translations.literal: And again: "Speech and conduct are the hinge of the gentleman; when the hinge moves, honor and disgrace are its master."
translations.idiomatic: And again: "Speech and conduct are the hinge of the gentleman; when the hinge moves, honor and disgrace follow."

sentences.zh: 當中宗棄代，韋氏奪權，預謀者十有九人，咸生異議，瓌誌存大節，獨發讜言。

translations.literal: When Emperor Zhongzong passed from the throne and the Wei clan seized power, of the nineteen who took part in the planning all raised differing views; Gui's purpose held to great integrity, and he alone spoke forthright words.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Zhongzong passed from the throne and the Wei clan seized power, of the nineteen who took part in the planning all raised differing views; Gui held to great integrity and alone spoke forthright words.

sentences.zh: 其後善惡顯彰，黜陟明著。

translations.literal: Afterward good and evil were clearly revealed, and demotions and promotions plainly shown.
translations.idiomatic: Afterward good and evil were clearly revealed, and demotions and promotions plainly shown.

sentences.zh: 聖人之言，驗於斯矣。

translations.literal: The sage's words were verified in this.
translations.idiomatic: The sage's words were verified in this.

sentences.zh: 頲唯公是相，以儉承家，李嶠許之湧泉，宋璟稱其過父。

translations.literal: Ting regarded only public duty in serving as minister, inherited the family with frugality; Li Jiao acknowledged his spring-like flow, Song Jing said he surpassed his father.
translations.idiomatic: Ting regarded only public duty in serving as minister and inherited the family tradition of frugality; Li Jiao acknowledged his thought flowed like a spring, and Song Jing said he surpassed his father.

sentences.zh: 艱難之際，節操不回，善始令終，先後無愧。

translations.literal: In times of difficulty his constancy did not bend; good beginning and fine end — as predecessor and successor without shame.
translations.idiomatic: In times of difficulty his constancy did not bend; he had a good beginning and a fine end—father and son alike without shame.

sentences.zh: 讚曰：善人君子，懷忠秉正。

translations.literal: Praise says: Good men and gentlemen, cherishing loyalty and upholding rectitude.
translations.idiomatic: Praise says: Good men and gentlemen, cherishing loyalty and upholding rectitude.

sentences.zh: 盡富文章，咸推諫諍。

translations.literal: Full of literary talent, all praised for remonstrance.
translations.idiomatic: Rich in literary talent, all praised for their remonstrance.

sentences.zh: 豈愧明廷，無慚重柄。

translations.literal: How could they shame the bright court? No shame in wielding great power.
translations.idiomatic: How could they shame the bright court? They felt no shame in wielding great power.

sentences.zh: 子子孫孫，演承餘慶。

translations.literal: Son after son, grandson after grandson, expanding inherited blessings.
translations.idiomatic: Son after son, grandson after grandson, they expanded the blessings they inherited.
